stem: The process of identifying and giving access to users is known as which of the following?
explanation: Authentication is the process of proving who a user is, for example with a username and password. Once the user is authenticated, authorization decides what that user may access.
whyWrong: Authorization decides what a user may do after the user has been identified.
Acceptance is not a term for identifying users and giving them access.
Administration is the general job of managing systems, not the process of proving identity.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 13: Users, Groups, and Permissions, Chapter Review question 1
note: 220-1102 2.1 (logical security); mapped to 220-1202 2.1 (logical security). The book's explanation describes the system account, so a correct explanation was written.

stem: The process that defines what an authenticated user may access and what they can do with the resources is known as which of the following?
explanation: Authorization for Windows files and folders is controlled by the NTFS file system, which assigns permissions to users and groups. These permissions define exactly what users may do to a resource on the system.
whyWrong: Restriction is not the formal term for what an authenticated user may do.
Authentication proves who a user is; it does not define what the user may access.
Administration is the general management of systems, not the process of granting access to resources.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 13: Users, Groups, and Permissions, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Fred wants to play World of Warcraft on his desktop system. He logs in and then the game asks for a code that is generated by an authenticator app on his Android phone. This is an example of ___________.
explanation: Using both a password and a security code is an example of multifactor authentication. The password is something Fred knows and the phone app is something he has.
whyWrong: Factor authorization is not a term; the code proves identity, which is authentication.
Authorization decides what the user may do, but the code is used to prove who the user is.
Factor authentication is not a term; using two or more factors is multifactor authentication.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 25: Maintaining and Securing Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 5
note: 220-1102 2.1; mapped to 220-1202 2.1 (logical security: MFA, authenticator application).

stem: Which of the following might offer good hardware authentication?
explanation: Smart cards are an example of hardware authentication devices. A smart card holds a chip with the user's credentials and is inserted into or tapped on a reader.
whyWrong: Strong passwords are something you know, not a hardware device.
Encrypted passwords are still passwords, not a hardware authentication device.
NTFS is a file system with permissions, not an authentication device.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 27: Securing Computers, Chapter Review question 2

stem: Which of the following is used for biometric authentication?
explanation: Palmprint scanners are a method of biometric authentication. Biometric devices identify a person by a physical feature, such as a palm print, fingerprint, or retina.
whyWrong: A motion sensor detects movement in an area; it does not identify a person.
An RSA token is something you have, not a biometric factor.
Kerberos is a network authentication protocol, not a biometric device.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 27: Securing Computers, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Which authentication factors are used to verify a person's identity? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: Unauthorized access can be prevented through the use of authentication. These authentication factors are something the user knows (knowledge factor), something the user has (possession factor), something the user does (behavioral factor), and somewhere the user is (location-based factor). Inherence is something the user is, such as a fingerprint or face.
whyWrong: Context describes the circumstances of a login, not an authentication factor.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 18

stem: Which of the following are examples of physical security? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: One-time password (OTP) tokens are usually implemented as hardware-based tokens that a person carries with them. The passcode changes periodically (for instance, every 60 seconds). A privacy filter is one that placed in front of a monitor to reduce the viewing angle and make it more difficult for shoulder surfers (social engineers) to discern information from the screen. Another example is an RSA token.
whyWrong: Directory permissions are logical rights in the operating system, not physical security.
The principle of least privilege is a logical security concept, not a physical object.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 22

stem: Which of the following will help protect an organization from further data exposure after a list of passwords has already been leaked due to a policy breach? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: You should implement a multifactor authentication system (such as one that uses usernames/passwords and also a smart card). You should also educate end users about company policies regarding the usage and storage of files and databases that can include passwords and personally identifiable information (PII).
whyWrong: Password strength was not the problem; the list of passwords itself was leaked.
File encryption protects stored data but does not strengthen authentication.
Restricted permissions do not help if the leaked list includes administrator passwords.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 24

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the primary focus of SAML, in the context of IAM and DLP?
options: Preventing the unauthorized copying or deletion of sensitive data after a user has been granted access
Managing and controlling user access to resources and systems based on their identity
Securely exchanging authentication and authorization data between an identity provider and a service provider to enable single sign-on
Storing and organizing user information like usernames, passwords, and access permissions within a directory service
explanation: The primary focus of SAML, in the context of IAM and DLP, is securely exchanging authentication and authorization data between an identity provider (IdP) and a service provider (SP) to enable single sign-on (SSO). Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) is an open standard used for authentication and authorization data exchange between an IdP and an SP, enabling SSO.
whyWrong: Preventing copying or deletion of sensitive data after access is the job of DLP.
Managing user access based on identity is the job of IAM as a whole.
Storing user information in a directory is the job of directory services.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 55

stem: You go to the store and put your bank card into an ATM and enter your PIN. What examples of multifactor authentication have you exhibited? (Select two.)
explanation: An automated teller machine (ATM) is a common example of a multifactor authentication system. Usually, an ATM requires “something you have” (your ATM card) and “something you know” (personal identification number [PIN]).
whyWrong: Something you are is a biometric factor, which an ATM card and PIN do not use.
Somewhere you are uses location, such as geofencing, which the ATM does not check.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 85

stem: What action should the systems administrator take to minimize the number of help desk tickets submitted, as reported by the manager regarding staff members frequently forgetting passwords for their mobile devices and applications?
options: Implement a single sign-on system with biometrics
explanation: To address the issue of staff members frequently forgetting their passwords, implementing a single sign-on system with biometrics can be an effective solution. This approach allows users to authenticate themselves using unique physical characteristics, such as fingerprints or facial recognition, reducing the reliance on memorizing passwords and minimizing the chances of forgetting them.
whyWrong: MFA adds security but still needs the passwords that users forget.
A higher failed-login threshold does not help users remember passwords.
Removing complex password rules weakens security.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 4

stem: What option from the list below can be utilized to establish secure physical access to a data center?
explanation: In order to ensure secure physical access to a data center, a proximity card reader can be employed. Proximity card readers utilize radio frequency identification (RFID) technology to grant authorized individuals access to restricted areas. These readers detect and validate proximity cards, also known as access cards or keycards, allowing entry to authorized personnel while restricting unauthorized individuals from entering the data center.
whyWrong: A perimeter barrier encloses the site but does not control who enters.
An intrusion detection system alerts on entry but does not control access.
A surveillance camera records activity but does not control access.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 21

stem: A high-street jewelry store needs to improve its physical security measures after a spate of ram-raids have hit similar businesses. To improve building security and prevent vehicles from driving into the premises while not impacting pedestrian access, which of the following options is MOST effective?
explanation: The best solution for enhancing building security while allowing easy customer access is to install protective barriers such as bollards. Bollards are sturdy posts or barriers strategically placed around the building perimeter to physically prevent vehicles from breaching the area. They provide an effective physical deterrent and minimize the risk of unauthorized vehicle access, ensuring the safety of the premises.
whyWrong: Security personnel can watch but cannot physically stop a vehicle.
Motion detectors detect movement but do not stop vehicles.
An access control vestibule controls people, not vehicles.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 42

stem: After a regulatory audit, an administrator is tasked with adding more security to the authentication process. The audit recommends deploying multi-factor authentication (MFA). Which method would BEST address this requirement?
explanation: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) involves the use of multiple authentication factors to verify the identity of a user. In this case, the combination of a one-time password (OTP) and a fingerprint scan serves as an example of MFA. The OTP provides a temporary code that is unique for each authentication attempt, adding an additional layer of security. Meanwhile, the fingerprint scan verifies the user’s biometric data, such as their unique fingerprint pattern, adding another layer of authentication.
whyWrong: Voice and facial recognition are both something you are, a single factor.
A username and password are both something you know.
A password and a PIN are both something you know.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 49

stem: Which of the following could be used for two-factor authentication?
explanation: Using a password and some kind of biometrics is an example of two-factor authentication, or 2FA. The password is something you know, and the biometric is something you are, so two different factor types are combined.
whyWrong: The IMEI identifies the phone and the IMSI identifies the subscriber; neither is an authentication factor.
GPS and location services track where a device is; they do not prove who the user is.
PRL and baseband updates keep a phone working on the carrier network; they do not authenticate users.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 29
note: From the Core 1 practice exam; multifactor authentication is a 220-1202 2.1 topic.

stem: There has recently been a string of hardware thefts in your office building. What should you recommend that your users implement to help avoid this problem?
explanation: Sometimes the only way to ensure that equipment doesn't walk away is to lock it down physically. Laptops come equipped with holes for cable locks that can be used to secure them to a desk or other workstation. GPS tracking might help after the device is stolen, but it's best to prevent that in the first place.
whyWrong: GPS tracking can help find a device after it is stolen, but it does not stop the theft.
A docking station connects a laptop to peripherals; it does not hold the laptop in place.
A screensaver lock protects the data on screen, but the hardware can still be carried away.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 9

stem: What is the primary purpose of two-factor authentication (2FA)?
options: To provide secure physical access to devices
To verify the identity of users with an additional authentication factor
To prevent unauthorized access to corporate applications
explanation: Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of security by requiring users to provide two different authentication factors to verify their identity. Secure physical access to devices is typically achieved through other means, such as biometric authentication or physical keys. The primary purpose of 2FA is to enhance identity verification, although it can indirectly help prevent unauthorized access to corporate applications.
whyWrong: Encryption in transit protects data on the network; 2FA checks who the user is at sign-in.
Physical access to devices is controlled by locks and badges, not by a second sign-in factor.
Blocking unauthorized access is a side effect; the purpose of 2FA is stronger identity verification.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 32
note: 220-1101 1.4 (2FA under mobile device management); mapped to 220-1202 2.1 (multifactor authentication).

stem: Which of the following types of authentication is two-factor? (Choose two.)
explanation: A password is “something you know” and a fingerprint is “something you are”. This is an example of two-factor authentication. Gait is something you do and a swiped card is something you have, so that pair also uses two different factor types. A retina and fingerprint are both “something you are”, and a password and PIN are both “something you know”.
whyWrong: A retina scan and a fingerprint are both something you are, so they are one factor type.
A password and a PIN are both something you know, so they are one factor type.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.4 question 2
note: 220-1101 1.4; mapped to 220-1202 2.1 (multifactor authentication). Book answer B corrected: the book says gait and swiping a card are both something you do, but a card is something you have, so option D also combines two factor types; the question now has two answers and the stem says (Choose two.).

stem: What can you use to prevent PII and sensitive data from being shared outside the company over corporate email?
explanation: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) prevents someone from sending an email containing PII and sensitive information. It blocks data if it finds a pattern match. A legal hold prevents users from deleting emails from a mailbox. A firewall is used to block traffic coming into or going out of your company’s networks.
whyWrong: A legal hold keeps mailbox items from being deleted; it does not stop data from being sent out.
MailTips warn senders about things like large distribution lists; they do not block sensitive content.
A firewall filters network traffic by address and port; it does not inspect email for PII patterns.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.4 question 17
note: 220-1101 1.4 (mobile device application support); mapped to 220-1202 2.1 (data loss prevention).

stem: Which component of physical security addresses outer-level access control?
explanation: Fences are intended to delay or deter entrance into a facility. Access control vestibules are used for mid-layer access control to prevent tailgating. Multifactor authentication is used for mid- and inner-layer access control. Strong passwords are used for mid- and inner-layer access control.
whyWrong: An access control vestibule controls entry at the middle layer and stops tailgating, not at the outer perimeter.
Multifactor authentication protects the middle and inner layers, such as systems and rooms, not the outer boundary.
Strong passwords protect logical access at the inner layers, not the physical outer perimeter of a site.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 1

stem: Which type of device can detect weapons on a person entering a facility?
explanation: A magnetometer, also known as a metal detector, can detect weapons on a person entering a facility. Biometrics are used to authenticate someone based on their face, retina, fingerprint, or some other method that biologically verifies their identity. A motion sensor is used to detect motion. A badge reader is used to scan security ID badges.
whyWrong: Biometric devices verify identity from a physical trait; they cannot find hidden weapons.
A motion sensor detects movement in an area; it does not detect metal objects on a person.
A badge reader scans ID badges to grant entry; it does not detect weapons.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 2

stem: You're in the process of securing the IT infrastructure by adding fingerprint scanners to your existing authentication methods. This type of security is an example of which of the following?
explanation: A fingerprint scanner, or any device that identifies a person by a physical trait, is considered a biometric security control. Access control is the system that controls access for users. Physical barriers are structures that limit physical access. Softening refers to weakening of security.
whyWrong: Access control is the overall system of granting access; a fingerprint scanner is specifically a biometric control.
Physical barriers such as fences limit physical movement; they do not identify a person by a trait.
Softening means weakening security, which is the opposite of adding fingerprint scanners.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 4

stem: A vice president of your company calls a meeting with the IT department after a recent trip to competitors’ sites. She reports that many of the companies she visited granted access to the operating system or applications after an employee presented a number that rotated. Of the following, which technology relies on a rotating number for users for authentication?
explanation: Tokens are rotating numerical keys that you must physically have with you to gain access to the operating system or applications. Biometrics relies on a physical characteristic of the user to verify identity. Smartcards contain a private certificate key and are protected with a password. Geofencing uses your GPS coordinates to ensure that the authentication happens when you are in a defined geographic area.
whyWrong: A smartcard holds a certificate and a private key protected by a PIN; it does not show a rotating number.
Biometrics verifies a physical trait such as a fingerprint, not a rotating number.
Geofencing checks the GPS location of a device; it does not use a rotating number.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 7

stem: Which is an example of an authentication method in which you have something?
explanation: A key fob is an example of authentication for something you have. A password is something you know. A fingerprint is something you are. A place is a geographical place in which you are.
whyWrong: A password is something you know, not something you have.
A fingerprint is something you are, not something you have.
A place is somewhere you are, which is a location factor, not something you have.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 13

stem: Which of the following has the goal of allowing a username/password combination to be entered once and then allowing claims to be used for consecutive logins? (Choose the BEST answer.)
explanation: The goal of single sign-on (SSO) is to allow a username/password combination. Once the combination is entered, claims are used to access additional resources. Tokens are given to the operating system after a user successfully logs in; they allow a user to access rights on the operating system. Kerberos is used (along with Active Directory) to authenticate a user on the Windows operating system. Multifactor authentication is the use of two or more factors to authenticate a user.
whyWrong: Tokens are given to a user after login to carry rights; they are not the sign-in-once method itself.
Kerberos is the protocol that authenticates domain users; single sign-on is the goal described here.
Multifactor authentication uses two or more factors; it does not reuse one login for later resources.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 7

stem: Which of the following is the science of recognizing humans based on physical characteristics?
explanation: Biometrics is the science of recognizing humans based on physical characteristics. In the authentication world, it falls into the category of “something a person is.” Access control vestibules (also known as mantraps) are implemented to stop tailgating. CAC, which stands for Common Access Card, is a card used by defense personnel, such as DoD employees.
whyWrong: An access control vestibule (mantrap) is a two-door space that stops tailgating; it does not recognize body traits.
Tailgating is a social engineering attack where someone follows an authorized person through a secure door.
A Common Access Card is a smart card for defense staff, which is something you have, not a physical trait.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 43: Physical Security, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: You have been tasked with preventing unwanted removal of a webcam. Which of the following tools should you implement?
explanation: Use a USB lock to prevent the removal of USB-based devices such as external USB storage drives, keyboards, mice, and webcams. Smart cards and USB-based fingerprint scanners are ways to authenticate a user to the computer or network. A privacy filter is used to prevent shoulder surfing—in which a person attempts to watch what a user is typing/performing in a system—by reducing the viewing angle.
whyWrong: A smart card authenticates a user to a computer or network; it does not lock a device to a port.
A USB fingerprint scanner authenticates users by fingerprint; it does not stop a webcam from being unplugged.
A privacy filter narrows the viewing angle of a screen to stop shoulder surfing, not device removal.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 43: Physical Security, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You want to know if there is any intrusion to your organization’s building. Which of the following should you implement? (Select the two BEST answers.)
explanation: Video surveillance and alarm systems can help to let you know if an intrusion occurs. However, they differ in that a video surveillance is often passive in design. It usually requires a person to actively monitor it. An alarm system, on the other hand, will trigger an alarm and then send an alert to a monitoring company, which will in turn notify the appropriate personnel at the organization that has been intruded upon.
whyWrong: A magnetometer detects metal objects on a person; it does not report a break-in to the building.
A standard door lock deters entry, but if it is bypassed it does not notify anyone of the intrusion.
Proper lighting deters intruders, but it is passive and does not alert anyone without added sensors.
An access control vestibule detains people between two doors; by itself it does not alert anyone.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 43: Physical Security, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: What is the primary function of a bollard in physical security?
options: To detect metal objects on individuals entering a building
To restrict vehicle access and protect buildings or walkways
To sound an alarm in case of unauthorized entry
To monitor and record video footage of the premises
explanation: Bollards are short, sturdy posts that are strategically placed to prevent vehicles from entering certain areas, such as pedestrian walkways or building entrances, while still allowing foot traffic to pass through. A magnetometer (metal detector) is used to detect metal objects on a person. Neither an alarm system nor a video surveillance system would include bollards.
whyWrong: A magnetometer, or metal detector, finds metal objects on people; a bollard is a post that blocks vehicles.
An alarm system sounds and sends alerts on unauthorized entry; bollards are passive posts with no alarm.
Video surveillance records the premises with cameras; a bollard is a physical barrier for vehicles.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 43: Physical Security, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which of the following is NOT a type of biometric authentication?
explanation: Keycard access is not a type of biometric authentication because it does not rely on unique biological traits for identification. Biometric authentication methods, such as fingerprint scanning, iris scanning, and voice recognition, use distinctive biological characteristics to verify an individual's identity.
whyWrong: Fingerprint scanning reads a unique physical trait, so it is a biometric method.
Iris scanning reads the unique pattern of the eye, so it is a biometric method.
Voice recognition identifies a person by the unique traits of the voice, so it is a biometric method.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 43: Physical Security, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: When is a Windows computer completely secure?
options: When you have updated to the latest version
When you have locked down the Local Security Policy
When Microsoft releases the latest update
explanation: Neither Windows nor any other technology is ever completely secure. Complete security is impossible. But you can reduce risk to a certain extent by configuring a system properly and by using technology wisely—ultimately providing relative security. Updating to the latest version is often a good idea (if done according to organization policy), but you can’t rely on software updates alone. A combination of security updates, security configurations, and user education should be part of an overall security plan.
whyWrong: Updates reduce risk, but no update makes a system completely secure on its own.
The Local Security Policy helps lock down a system, but it is only one layer of protection.
New Microsoft updates fix known flaws, but new threats keep appearing, so security is never complete.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 44: Logical Security, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: You are moving up in the world and have been tasked with securing a server room. Your manager tells you to design a system that will implement two-factor authentication. Which of the following should you use as your solution to provide the BEST level of security for the server room?
options: A security guard and an entry control roster
A biometric lock and hardware tokens
A door lock and an access control vestibule
A server cabinet lock and badge readers
explanation: The most secure solution listed is the biometric lock and hardware tokens. This solution combines two factors of authentication: biometrics (something you are) and hardware tokens (something you have). While the other answers are good security methods, they do not incorporate two factors of authentication, and so they do not provide enough security for today’s typical organization. Remember the phrase defense in depth, which means layered security. The more layers you have (within reason), the more secure your environment will be.
whyWrong: A security guard and an entry roster both check identity, but they do not combine two authentication factors.
A door lock and an access control vestibule are both physical barriers, not two different authentication factors.
A cabinet lock and badge readers are good controls, but they do not form two-factor authentication for the room.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 44: Logical Security, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the primary purpose of just-in-time access?
options: Providing permanent access to all network resources
Granting temporary privileged access only when needed
Encrypting all data stored on network servers
Implementing two-factor authentication for all users
explanation: Just-in-time access is designed to minimize security risks by granting access to resources only when necessary and for the shortest possible time. This reduces the window of opportunity for attackers to exploit compromised credentials. Providing permanent access to all network resources is the opposite of just-in-time access, which seeks to eliminate standing privileges. Although encrypting all stored data is great, it’s not the primary function of just-in-time access. Two-factor authentication is also great, but not the purpose of just-in-time access.
whyWrong: Permanent access to every resource is the standing privilege that just-in-time access is meant to remove.
Encrypting stored data protects data at rest; it is not the purpose of just-in-time access.
Two-factor authentication verifies identity with two factors; it is not about time-limited privileges.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 44: Logical Security, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: What is the primary function of authentication in the context of identity and access management (IAM)?
options: Determining what resources a user is allowed to access
Preventing data loss through unauthorized transfers
Monitoring network traffic for malicious activity
explanation: Verifying a user’s identity is the primary function of IAM. This is typically done through passwords, biometrics, or other means. Determining what resources a user is allowed access to is authorization, not authentication. Preventing data loss through unauthorized transfers is the role of data loss prevention (DLP). Monitoring network traffic for malicious activity is handled by intrusion detection systems and intrusion prevention systems (IDS/IPS), which are advanced firewall systems.
whyWrong: Deciding which resources a user may access is authorization, which comes after authentication.
Stopping unauthorized data transfers is the job of data loss prevention, not authentication.
Watching network traffic for malicious activity is the job of IDS and IPS systems, not authentication.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 44: Logical Security, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: What is the purpose of a motion sensor in a security system?
options: To detect the presence of unauthorized individuals or objects
To control the temperature of the surrounding environment
To amplify the sound of nearby movements
To adjust the brightness of the lighting system
explanation: Motion sensors are primarily designed to detect any movement within their range. They are commonly used in security systems to identify the presence of unauthorized individuals or objects, trigger an alarm, or activate other security measures.
whyWrong: Controlling temperature is the job of an HVAC system, not of a motion sensor in a security system.
Motion sensors detect movement; they do not amplify sound, which would be audio equipment.
Adjusting lighting brightness is the job of a photosensor or dimmer, not of a motion sensor.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 1

stem: A CISO is proposing to use an app on company-deployed smartphones as a soft token. What is the purpose of a soft token?
explanation: Soft tokens are software-based security tokens that generate one-time passwords (OTPs) to authenticate the user’s identity during the login process. They are commonly used in logical security systems to provide an additional layer of security. Soft tokens generate unique passwords that are valid for a short period of time, ensuring that only authorized users can access sensitive information or perform specific actions.
whyWrong: A soft token produces short-lived one-time codes for login, not long-term secure passwords for the user to keep.
A soft token does not encrypt data; its codes only prove the identity of the user at login.
Blocking malicious websites is done by content filters, not by a soft token used for authentication.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 2

stem: A chief information security manager (CISO) is reviewing the security controls that will best prevent a user from gaining unauthorized physical access to the server room. What two controls would BEST address this requirement?
explanation: Physical controls are designed to prevent unauthorized access to facilities and information systems. An access control vestibule forces a user to enter a small space (designed for only one person), with interlocking doors to enforce security. The user must provide authentication before being allowed access through the second door. Door locks prevent unauthorized users from gaining access.
whyWrong: An alarm detects an intrusion after it happens but does not prevent entry to the server room.
Video surveillance records and detects intrusion but does not physically stop anyone from entering.
Bollards stop vehicles from ramming a building or perimeter; they do not control access to a room.
Motion sensors detect movement inside a space but do not prevent a person from getting in.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 4

stem: A cloud service provider (CSP) has recently added a number of security controls in response to a recent security audit. These controls have required the installation of perimeter fencing and security gates and additional guards to be employed to secure all external entry points. The audit also highlighted the lack of detective controls, within the CSP data center, in the event the perimeter security is breached. What detective controls would BEST address this requirement? (Choose two.)
explanation: Detective controls would allow the security staff to be aware of breaches that evaded the physical security controls. This is referred to as defense in depth. Video surveillance and motion sensors would allow a security team to detect unauthorized intrusion.
whyWrong: An access control vestibule is a preventive control that stops entry; it does not detect a breach.
A badge reader is a preventive control that grants or denies entry rather than detecting an intrusion.
Equipment locks prevent hardware from being taken but do not alert anyone to an intruder.
Door locks prevent entry and are preventive controls, not detective controls.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 5

stem: A security team must design controls to ensure the business will be compliant with stringent requirements regarding safeguarding customer payment card details. Servers hosting customer card payment details will be physically secured in a server room. Access to the server room needs to be controlled using two-factor authentication (2FA). Currently, administrators access the server room using a fingerprint reader. What could be used in addition to fingerprints to support two-factor access control?
explanation: To support two-factor authentication (2FA), you cannot choose another factor from the same group. A smart card is a physical device; it is something you have. Retina scanners and palmprint scanners are both considered biometrics, or something you are, in the same category as a fingerprint reader.
whyWrong: A retina scanner is a biometric, the same factor group as the fingerprint reader already in use.
A palmprint scanner is also something you are, so it adds no second factor to the fingerprint.
A motion detector senses movement in a room and is not an authentication method at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 6

stem: A security team is evaluating additional security controls to ensure physical equipment, including storage devices, cannot be removed by authorized members of staff from the internal data center. What control would allow security guards to be alerted if there is an attempt to remove equipment from the data center?
explanation: Magnetometers are devices that can detect concealed metallic objects. This technology can be deployed at access points to the data center. Equipment can also be tagged in order to sound an alert on the magnetometer.
whyWrong: An access control vestibule controls who enters and does not detect equipment being carried out.
Video surveillance may miss equipment that is hidden under a jacket or other clothing.
Equipment locks prevent removal, but the requirement here is a detective control that raises alerts.
Lighting helps video surveillance work well but does not detect hidden equipment on its own.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 7

stem: A network administrator onboards a new user who has joined the sales team as a junior sales executive. They have created a unique account for the user and added the user to a security group with limited access rights. What BEST describes why this process would be adopted?
options: To adhere to the principle of least privilege
To ensure the user is using multifactor authentication (MFA)
To support the use of organizational units
explanation: Adding a user to a group with security restrictions would adhere to the principle of least privilege. The user gets only the access rights needed for the junior sales role, which limits the damage if the account is misused.
whyWrong: ACLs set who may access a resource, but the reason for limited group rights is least privilege.
Adding a user to a restricted security group has nothing to do with multifactor authentication.
Organizational units organize objects for Group Policy and administration, not to limit access rights.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 8

stem: When a user needs to access company assets from a laptop computer, they must have access to an app on their mobile phone. The app provides a time-based one-time password (TOTP) that must be provided along with a log-in ID and password. What BEST describes the technology used? (Choose two.)
explanation: MFA requires the use of two or more authentication factors when logging on to their user account. There are three main groups: something you know, something you have, and something you are. In this case, the user used something they knew (password) and an authenticator app on the phone that generates TOTP codes, which is something you have.
whyWrong: Least privilege limits account rights and does not describe a login that adds a one-time code.
SMS sends a code in a text message, but here an app generates the code on the phone.
Voice call verification reads a code in a phone call, which is not what the user does here.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 10
note: 220-1102 2.1; mapped to 220-1202 2.1 (physical and logical security). The book explanation calls the app a hardware token; it is an authenticator app (soft token), so that sentence is reworded.

stem: A bank needs to ensure customers can provide an additional authentication factor when authorizing payments during online banking. The bank intends to support this using a second out-of-band mobile phone authentication. What 2FA methods require the user to have access to a mobile phone? (Choose two.)
explanation: Voice call verification requires a user to take a call from a phone (including a mobile), and SMS messages require the user to validate a code sent to their mobile device. Both are out-of-band methods that depend on the user having the phone.
whyWrong: An email verification link can be received on any computer without access to a mobile phone.
A hard token is a separate security device, such as a USB key or key fob, not a mobile phone.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 12

stem: What does NTFS use to provide security for individual files and folders?
explanation: Because NTFS views individual files and folders as objects, it can provide security for those objects through an Access control list. Each entry in the access control list grants or denies an NTFS permission to a user or group.
whyWrong: Dynamic disks let volumes span drives; they do not secure files and folders.
ECC is error-correcting memory, not a file system security feature.
The MFT is the NTFS table that tracks files; it does not by itself set who can access them.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 9: Implementing Mass Storage, Chapter Review question 4

stem: Which of the following is a unique combination of a username and an associated password stored in a database on your computer?
explanation: Security begins with a user account, a unique combination of a username and an associated password, stored in a database on the computer, that grants the user access to the system. Windows checks the user account each time someone signs in to decide whether to grant access.
whyWrong: A group holds user accounts; it is not a username and password combination.
Power Users is a built-in group, not a username and password record.
User information is not the term for a username with its password.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 13: Users, Groups, and Permissions, Chapter Review question 2

stem: Which of the following is the name of a container that holds user accounts and defines the capabilities of its users?
explanation: A single group account can be a member of multiple groups. Groups are an efficient way of managing multiple users, especially when you are dealing with a whole network of accounts.
whyWrong: Users is the name of one built-in group, not the general name for a container of accounts.
Storage holds data; it does not hold user accounts or define their capabilities.
RAM is computer memory, not a container for user accounts.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 13: Users, Groups, and Permissions, Chapter Review question 4

stem: Which of the following refers to administrative privileges that provide complete control over a machine?
explanation: Administrator privileges grant complete control over a machine. It is common for the primary user of a Windows system to have their account linked to the Administrators group.
whyWrong: Standard user-level privileges limit what an account can change on the system.
Power Users privileges are almost, but not quite, as powerful as an administrator's.
Standard user privileges allow normal work but block system-wide changes.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 13: Users, Groups, and Permissions, Chapter Review question 5

stem: Almost as powerful as members of the Administrators group, members of which group cannot install new devices or access other users’ files or folders unless the files or folders specifically provide them access?
explanation: Almost as powerful as members of the Administrators group, members of the Power Users group cannot install new devices or access other users’ files or folders unless the files or folders specifically provide them access. Microsoft keeps the Power Users group in current Windows only so that older programs still work.
whyWrong: The Users group is far more limited and cannot make system-wide changes.
The Administrators group is the more powerful group that the stem compares against.
Standard User is a type of account, not the legacy group described here.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 13: Users, Groups, and Permissions, Chapter Review question 6
note: 220-1102 2.5; mapped to 220-1202 2.2 (users and groups). The book key gives B (Administrator group), but its own explanation names the Power Users group, so the answer was set to Power Users. Power Users exists in Windows only for backward compatibility.

stem: Which types of groups cannot edit the Registry or access system files. They can create groups but may only manage those they create.
explanation: User groups cannot edit the Registry or access system files. They can create groups but may only manage those they create. New user accounts in Windows are added to the Users group by default.
whyWrong: Members of the Administrators group can edit the Registry and access system files.
Power Users have more rights than the Users group and are almost as powerful as administrators.
Standard User is an account type, not the name of a Windows group.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 13: Users, Groups, and Permissions, Chapter Review question 7

stem: Which of these is not a requirement for using fingerprint authentication in Windows?
options: Logging in with a PIN number
Logging in with a Microsoft account
Repeatedly placing your finger on the scanner
explanation: Users will have to use a Microsoft account, set up a PIN, and repeatedly place their finger on the scanner in order to use fingerprint authentication. After setup, the user can sign in with the fingerprint and keep the PIN as a backup.
whyWrong: Windows Hello requires a PIN to be set up before a fingerprint can be added.
The book lists a Microsoft account as a requirement for Windows Hello fingerprint sign-in.
Enrolling a fingerprint requires placing the finger on the scanner several times.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 13: Users, Groups, and Permissions, Chapter Review question 8
note: 220-1102 2.5; mapped to 220-1202 2.2 (log-in OS options). In current Windows, Windows Hello also works with a local account.

stem: Which of the following defines exactly what any particular account can or cannot do to a file or folder?
explanation: NTFS permissions are the primary tool for authorization and provide many configuration options for user access and security. Examples include Full Control, Modify, Read & Execute, Read, and Write.
whyWrong: Admin permissions is not the name of the Windows file and folder permission system.
User permissions is not the formal term; NTFS permissions are set for users and groups.
Group permissions is not a separate system; groups receive NTFS permissions like users do.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 13: Users, Groups, and Permissions, Chapter Review question 9

stem: Which of the following is an NTFS permission that enables an account to seize control of a file or folder?
explanation: Administrators have Take Ownership permission for everything and can use this to take ownership away from someone and then access their files. The new owner of a file or folder can then change its permissions.
whyWrong: Take Charge is not an NTFS permission.
Seize and Desist is not an NTFS permission.
Take Away is not an NTFS permission.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 13: Users, Groups, and Permissions, Chapter Review question 10

stem: One of your coworkers tells you that whenever they return to their desk, they have to type their username and password to unlock the computer. They say they cannot modify the screensaver. After analyzing the system, you notice that the screensaver and the screen lock options are indeed grayed out. Which of the following is the MOST LIKELY reason for this?
explanation: The most likely reason for this is that domain-level group policies have been implemented by the administrator. This is by design so that end users cannot change the screensaver and screen lock settings. This policy cannot be changed by the end user.
whyWrong: Local policies could do this, but grayed-out options on a domain computer point to domain policy.
Antivirus policies affect the antivirus software, not Windows screensaver settings.
A corrupted Registry would cause errors, not a neat set of locked security options.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 7

stem: Jenny from accounting reports that when pressing Ctrl+Alt+Del to log on to a Windows workstation, she is asked for a PIN. Which of the following should you tell Jenny?
options: “Enter all the passwords that you have used previously.”
“Please verify that you are using your smart card.”
explanation: You should tell Jenny to make sure she is using her smart card. In a multifactor authentication system, you might have a combination of a physical smart card requiring that a personal identification number (PIN) be typed and then the password. So, you want to make sure that users are swiping (or inserting) their smart card before entering the PIN code. Of course, it depends on the type of authentication (or MFA) system that is in place. In this scenario, and with the answers listed, verification of the user’s smart card is the best answer.
whyWrong: Entering old passwords is poor advice, and the prompt is asking for a PIN, not a password.
A reboot will bring back the same PIN prompt.
The network cable has nothing to do with a PIN prompt at logon.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 19
note: Smart cards are listed under 220-1202 2.1 (physical access security); the PIN prompt is a log-in option of 2.2.

stem: By default, a file or folder receives its NTFS permissions from the parent folder. Which of the following terms is used for this process?
explanation: Inheritance means that a file or folder receives its NTFS permissions from the parent folder. It is the default setting of the Advanced configuration dialog box within the Security tab of a file or folder. In Windows, it is shown as a button that can enable or disable inheritance.
whyWrong: Propagation is when a parent folder pushes its permissions down to subfolders, a separate setting.
Single sign-on uses one login for many resources; it is not about NTFS permissions.
Client-side virtualization runs operating systems in virtual machines.
Proxy settings send web traffic through a go-between server.
A recovery image restores an operating system after a failure.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 21

stem: A customer reports to you that a file shared on their computer for another user is not accessible to that third party. The customer says that the third party was given Allow rights for Read and Write access to the file. Which of the following could be a reason the third party cannot access the file?
options: The parent folder has explicit Allow rights set for the third-party user.
The parent folder has explicit Deny rights set for the third-party user.
The user forgot to share the parent folder and shared only the specific file.
The parent folder likely has the archive attribute enabled.
explanation: The best answer listed is that the parent folder has explicit Deny rights set for the third-party user. If this is the case, then by default, that permission will propagate to any subfolders and files within the parent. This can also be expressed as the default action for a subfolder (also known as a child folder) to inherit its permissions from the parent. Basically, you should remember two things: A folder inherits its permissions from the parent, and Deny rights will always override Allow rights.
whyWrong: Explicit Allow rights on the parent would let the third party access the file.
Windows shares folders, not single files, so this cannot be the cause.
The archive attribute marks a file for backup; it does not block access.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 65

stem: A user wants to protect all of the data at rest on a Windows laptop. You analyze the laptop and find that it has a TPM chip. Which of the following should you use to secure the data while taking advantage of the TPM?
explanation: Use BitLocker to encrypt the data on the laptop. As long as the laptop has a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) chip (or uses USB keys), BitLocker can be implemented to encrypt entire volumes/drives (data at rest) using AES.
whyWrong: SFTP protects data in motion during file transfers, not data at rest.
ACLs allow or deny access; they do not encrypt data.
EFS encrypts single files and folders and does not use the TPM.
A hardware security module is a separate device or card, not the built-in TPM.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 90

stem: A technician inserts an encrypted USB drive protected with BitLocker. When attempting to access the files on the USB drive through File Explorer, the technician encounters an error message stating that the drive is locked. Which of the following tools should the technician use to unlock and gain access to the encrypted drive?
explanation: The technician should use the BitLocker Drive Encryption tool to unlock and access the encrypted USB drive. By entering the decryption key or password in the BitLocker Drive Encryption settings, the drive can be unlocked, allowing authorized access to the files stored on it while ensuring data security.
whyWrong: Disk Clean-up frees space by deleting unneeded files; it cannot unlock an encrypted drive.
Windows Defender Firewall filters network traffic and has no role in drive encryption.
Task Scheduler runs programs at set times or events; it does not unlock drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.4 question 15

stem: A user was issued with a new laptop computer running Windows 10. They raised a ticket with the help desk as their fingerprint reader is now not working following a recent Windows update. Which of the following is the NEXT step?
explanation: Updates often install new drivers that load only after a restart, so rebooting the laptop is the simple next step when the fingerprint reader stops working after a Windows update. If the problem remains, the technician can reinstall or roll back the biometric driver and set up the fingerprint again in Windows Hello. Clearing the TPM deletes the keys it stores, so it is a last resort.
whyWrong: A BIOS update is a larger change and does not address a driver problem left by a Windows update.
Clearing the TPM erases the keys stored in it, including Windows Hello and BitLocker keys, and is not a first fix.
Restoring a system image is a drastic step that loses recent changes and is not needed yet.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.2 question 8
note: 220-1101 5.2; mapped to 220-1202 2.2 (log-in OS options, Windows Hello fingerprint). Book answer B corrected: clearing the TPM deletes the keys stored in it (Windows Hello credentials, BitLocker keys) and is a last resort; a restart that completes the update and reloads the biometric driver is the simple next step.

stem: Which Active Directory component maps printers and drives during login?
explanation: A login script is used by Active Directory during login to map drives and printers. A home folder is a private network location in which the user can store their personal files. Organizational units (OUs) are used to group computers and users so that Group Policy can be applied. The MMC is used to manage various aspects of Active Directory and the local operating system.
whyWrong: A home folder is a private network location for a user's files; it does not map drives and printers.
An organizational unit groups users and computers for Group Policy; it does not run at login.
The MMC is a management console for administrators; it does not run at user login.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 20

stem: You want to follow the rules of good security administration as set by CompTIA and vendors. To do so, which account should be disabled on most Windows operating systems for security reasons?
explanation: The Guest account should be disabled on the operating system, unless there is good reason to leave the account enabled. Print Operators is a group found on Windows servers. Power Users is a group found on both Windows workstations and servers. Unless the user has left the organization, there should be no reason to disable the account.
whyWrong: Print Operators is a server group for managing printers, not a default account to disable.
Power Users is a group kept for compatibility, not the account that best practice says to disable.
Userone is a normal user account, which is disabled only when that person leaves.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which Windows feature helps protect against unauthorized changes to system files?
explanation: User Account Control (UAC) helps protect against unauthorized changes to system files by prompting for administrative approval. BitLocker and EFS provide encryption. Windows Defender offers antivirus protection.
whyWrong: BitLocker encrypts whole drives; it does not ask for approval before system changes.
EFS encrypts individual files and folders; it does not block unauthorized changes to system files.
Windows Defender protects against malware; it is not the prompt that asks for administrative approval.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 6

stem: You need to encrypt a single file on a Windows desktop. Which technology should you use?
explanation: The Encrypted File System (EFS) is a functionality of the Windows NTFS filesystem. EFS can encrypt individual files and folders. BitLocker is a full-device encryption technology. NTFS is a filesystem that supports encryption and security, among other functionality. BitLocker to Go is used for full-device encryption of removable drives.
whyWrong: BitLocker encrypts an entire drive, not one single file.
NTFS is the file system that supports EFS, not the encryption technology itself.
BitLocker to Go encrypts entire removable drives, not one file on the desktop.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 15

stem: A user is in both the Sales group and the Marketing group. The Sales group has full permission at the share level, and the Marketing group has Read-only permission. The files on NTFS are secured with the Modify permission for the Sales group and the Read & Execute permission for the Marketing group. Which permissions will the user have?
explanation: Because the user is in both groups and the Sales group has full share permissions and the Sales group has modify NTFS permissions, the most restrictive of the two is Modify, so that will be the effective permission for the user. All of the other answers are incorrect. Within each level the permissions of the groups combine, so the user gets Full at the share and Modify on NTFS.
whyWrong: Full is the combined share permission, but the more restrictive NTFS Modify permission applies.
Read-only is the Marketing share permission, but the Sales group grants Full at the share level.
Read & Execute is the Marketing NTFS permission, but the Sales group grants Modify, which is higher.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 16

stem: James just moved a folder on the same partition. What will happen with the permissions for the folder?
options: The permissions will be the same as they were before the move.
The permissions will be inherited from the new parent folder.
The permissions will be configured as the root folder for the drive letter.
The permissions will be blank until configured.
explanation: The permissions will be the same as before the move, since you are just moving the files and not creating a new entity. The permissions will not be inherited from the parent folder. The permissions will not be configured the same as the root folder. The permissions will not be blank.
whyWrong: Permissions are inherited from the new parent only when a folder is copied or moved to another partition.
A moved folder does not take the permissions of the drive's root folder.
A moved folder keeps its permissions; they do not become blank.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 17

stem: A user is in the Sales group. The Sales group has no permissions at the share level. The files on NTFS are secured with the Modify permission for the Sales group. What permissions will the user have?
options: The user will have the Modify permission when connecting from the network.
The user will have the Modify permission when logged in locally to the computer.
The user will have no access when logged in locally to the computer.
The user will have Read-only permissions when connecting from the network.
explanation: The user will have only the Modify permission when logged in locally to the computer, since the filesystem is not shared with the appropriate permissions. The user will not have the Modify permission when connecting from the network. The user will still have the Modify permission when logged in locally, because of the NTFS permissions. The user will not have read-only permissions when connecting from the network.
whyWrong: With no share permissions the user has no access from the network, even with NTFS Modify.
Local access uses only the NTFS permissions, so the user has Modify, not no access.
With no share permissions the user cannot reach the files from the network at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 18

stem: You are trying to delete a file on the local filesystem, but the operating system will not let you. What could be the problem? (Choose the BEST answer.)
options: The NTFS Modify permission is applied to the file.
The share permissions are not set to Full Control.
The file attributes are set to Read-only.
The file attributes are set to System.
explanation: The file attributes are most likely set to Read-only, and thus you are not permitted to delete the file. The Modify permission would not hinder the file from being deleted. The share permissions would not have any bearing on the problem, since the local filesystem is being accessed. The file attributes being set to System would not restrict a file from being deleted.
whyWrong: The NTFS Modify permission includes the right to delete, so it would not block the deletion.
Share permissions do not apply when the file is accessed on the local file system.
The System attribute marks an operating system file but does not stop it from being deleted.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 19

stem: Which of the following programs could be considered antimalware?
explanation: Windows Defender Security is considered antimalware and antivirus protection for the Windows operating system. Mobile device management (MDM) software is used to manage mobile devices. Windows Action Center is a notification center for action to be taken in the operating system. VirusTotal is a third-party site that analyzes virus signatures, but it does not protect you from them.
whyWrong: MDM software manages and secures mobile devices; it is not antimalware software.
Windows Action Center shows notifications and quick settings; it does not remove malware.
VirusTotal is a website that analyzes files for malware but does not protect a computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 13

stem: You have been tasked with setting up encryption for a Windows computer. You are required to encrypt several shared folders within a partition so that they can’t be read by other users. What tool should you use?
explanation: Use Encrypting File System (EFS). This is easily done: Right-click the folder(s), select Properties, click the Advanced button, and check Encrypt contents to secure data. At this point, other users will not be able to read the files contained in those folders. BitLocker is used to encrypt an entire storage drive (or volume), but in the scenario, you only need to encrypt several folders. Regardless, administrative shares do not encrypt data.
whyWrong: BitLocker encrypts an entire drive or volume, not just several chosen folders.
A TPM chip stores keys for BitLocker; it is hardware, not a tool for encrypting folders.
An administrative share hides a share from casual users but does not encrypt any data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: One of the users on your network is trying to access files shared on a remote computer. The file’s share permissions allow the user Full Control, but the NTFS permissions allow the user Read access. Which of the following will be the resulting access for the user?
explanation: The user will get only Read access. If you are using both sets of permissions, the most restrictive set will take precedence. In this case, NTFS permissions are more restrictive than share permissions.
whyWrong: Full Control is the share permission, but the more restrictive NTFS Read permission wins.
Modify was not granted by either set of permissions, so the user cannot get it.
Write was not granted by either set; the user gets only the more restrictive Read access.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You are the administrator for your network, and you set up an administrative share called Data$. Which of the following are necessary for another user to access this share? (Select the two BEST answers.)
options: The user must have permissions to access the share.
The user must know the decryption key.
The user must know the exact network path to the share.
The user must enable File Sharing in the Network and Sharing Center.
explanation: The user needs to have permissions to the share and must know the exact path to the network share because it is an administrative share. The question does not mention whether the file is encrypted. The user doesn’t need to enable sharing; the person is trying to access a share.
whyWrong: The question does not say the share is encrypted, so no decryption key is needed.
The user only connects to the share; enabling File Sharing is needed on the computer that shares it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: You are tasked with encrypting several laptops using BitLocker. However, some of the laptops do not have a built-in TPM chip. What should you implement to enable BitLocker on those laptops?
explanation: If the laptops don’t have a TPM chip, use a USB key to provide the encryption required by BitLocker. A firmware update won’t help in this scenario; the TPM chip is an actual piece of hardware that is integrated to the motherboard. MFA stands for multifactor authentication. While MFA is a good idea, this question deals with encryption, not authentication. Encrypting the local drive is the task at hand, but you need to get BitLocker to work first!
whyWrong: A firmware update cannot add a TPM, because the TPM is a hardware chip on the motherboard.
MFA adds authentication factors; it does not supply the key storage that BitLocker needs.
Encrypting the local drive is the goal itself; BitLocker still needs a TPM or a USB key first.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which Windows account would you create for someone who needs to regularly install software, change settings, and take ownership?
explanation: Administrators have full control of an operating system. Power users are included in Windows for backward compatibility with older versions and are seldom used. Standard users are the normal default accounts for people who can log on to the network. Guests have limited access to the system. A guest cannot install software or hardware, cannot change settings, cannot access any data, and cannot change the password.
whyWrong: Power Users exists only for backward compatibility and does not have full control of Windows.
A standard user cannot install most software or change system-wide settings.
A guest has very limited access and cannot install software or change settings.
Root is the superuser account in Linux and UNIX, not a Windows account type.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which of the following is a built-in security component of Windows?
explanation: User Account Control (UAC) adds a layer of security to Windows to protect against malware and user error. It asks for permission or administrator credentials before a program can make changes that need administrative rights.
whyWrong: Firefox is a third-party web browser that is not included in Windows and is not a security component.
Active Directory runs on Windows Server; it is a directory service, not a built-in client security feature.
MFA is a method that uses two or more factors; it is not a built-in Windows security component.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: You have been tasked with configuring a user account so that its folders and settings will follow the user to whatever computer the user logs on to within the domain. Which of the following should you configure?
options: Home folder mapped to a network drive
explanation: Configure a roaming profile for the user. The roaming profile is configured at the domain controller and allows the user to move from one computer to the next, and the user profile follows—as long as the user is logging on with the same username and password and logging on to the domain. Organizational units (OUs) provide a way of organizing users, computers, and policies. A logon script is designed to execute programs, features, and actions when a user logs on. The home folder is the default location where a user will save and download files; it can be either local or mapped to a network drive, the latter of which is preferred on a domain.
whyWrong: An OU organizes users, computers, and policies; it does not make a user's settings follow the user.
A logon script runs programs and actions at logon; it does not carry the user's folders and settings.
A home folder on a network drive stores files, but not the full set of the user's settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: You need to block users from installing programs in Windows. Of the following, what tool should you use?
explanation: Use the Group Policy Editor (Run > gpedit.msc) to make modifications to how (and whether) programs are installed to Windows. (There are a variety of other ways as well.) Run > wf.msc brings up Microsoft Defender Firewall with Advanced Security. The principle of least privilege is not a tool but a concept, which states that a user (or program) should only be given the access required to complete a task—and no more. Digital signatures are used to cryptographically “sign” emails so that users can verify that the emails came from known good sources.
whyWrong: wf.msc opens Microsoft Defender Firewall with Advanced Security, which does not control program installation.
The principle of least privilege is a concept, not a tool you run to block installations.
Digital signatures verify that emails or files come from known sources; they do not block installs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings, Cram Quiz question 8
note: Group Policy is not a named 220-1202 2.2 topic; mapped to 2.2 users and groups (restricting what standard users can do).

stem: What is the primary function of Windows Hello?
options: To manage user accounts and computer accounts
To provide passwordless authentication using biometrics or a PIN
To set up a firewall for network protection
explanation: Windows Hello is a feature that allows users to sign in to Windows using biometrics like fingerprint or facial recognition, or a PIN. It is a passwordless authentication method that aims to improve security and convenience. BitLocker is used for disk encryption, Active Directory is used for managing user accounts and computer accounts, and Microsoft Defender Firewall is used for network protection.
whyWrong: Encrypting an entire disk is the job of BitLocker, not Windows Hello.
Managing user and computer accounts is the job of Active Directory, not Windows Hello.
Network protection is the job of Microsoft Defender Firewall, not Windows Hello.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings, Cram Quiz question 9

stem: What is the purpose of a roaming profile in Active Directory?
options: To allow users to access their files from any computer on the network
To execute specific tasks when a user logs on to the domain
To provide a centralized location for storing user documents
To store user settings and preferences on a server, allowing them to access a consistent profile from any computer on the domain
explanation: A roaming profile is a user profile stored on a server, allowing users to access their personalized settings and preferences from any computer on the domain. Home folders are used to store user documents, logon scripts execute tasks upon user login, and file sharing allows users to access files from other computers. Yes, allowing users to access their documents across computers connected to AD is a benefit of a roaming profile, but the primary purpose is to access one’s personalized settings and preferences across computers in the domain.
whyWrong: Reaching files from any computer is a side benefit; the main purpose is a consistent set of settings.
A logon script runs tasks when a user logs on to the domain; a roaming profile does not.
A home folder is the central place for user documents; a roaming profile carries settings and preferences.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings, Cram Quiz question 10

stem: An office installs a third-party antimalware suite on its Windows 11 workstations. To keep the two products from conflicting, a technician must turn off Microsoft Defender Antivirus real-time protection. Where in Windows Security is this setting?
options: Virus & threat protection, then Manage settings
explanation: Real-time protection is a Defender Antivirus setting, so it sits under Virus & threat protection in Windows Security. The Manage settings link there opens the toggles for real-time protection, cloud-delivered protection, and similar options. Turning real-time protection off lets the third-party product scan without the two engines fighting over files.
whyWrong: Firewall & network protection turns the Defender Firewall on or off for each network profile, not antivirus scanning.
App & browser control manages reputation-based protection such as SmartScreen, not the antivirus real-time engine.
Device performance & health reports on storage, battery, and updates; it has no antivirus scanning toggles.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

stem: A user wants to encrypt a USB flash drive with BitLocker To Go. Where does the user turn on encryption for the drive?
options: BitLocker Drive Encryption, the same place used for internal drives
Disk Management, by formatting the drive as NTFS
Device Manager, in the properties of the USB controller
Credential Manager, by adding a Windows credential
explanation: BitLocker To Go is the BitLocker feature for removable media such as USB drives. It is managed from BitLocker Drive Encryption, the same Control Panel item or Settings search used for internal drives. When the removable drive is inserted, it shows in that list and can be encrypted there.
whyWrong: Disk Management can format a drive, but formatting does not encrypt any of the data on it.
Device Manager handles drivers and hardware settings and has no option to encrypt a storage drive.
Credential Manager stores saved sign-in details; it does not encrypt removable drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings
