stem: When a user logs in to the Windows domain, an automated process is run that assigns the user a default storage location on a Windows server. The user is able to access this network link through the explorer interface. What describes this feature and how the system automates the creation of the link? (Choose two.)
explanation: Home folders give each user a unique storage location, hosted on a central server. Home folders are assigned using login scripts.
whyWrong: Managing security groups controls permissions and is not normally done when a user logs in.
Multifactor authentication secures sign-in with two or more factors; it does not map storage locations.
Organizational units organize Active Directory objects and do not create a storage link at login.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 9

stem: When a user authenticates their Active Directory account from any workstation, they can access all their common folders (Desktop, Documents, Pictures, and more). The folders contain all the up-to-date content that they saved. What two Windows features allow for centralized storage of user data and transparent network access to this data?
explanation: Group Policy is used to ensure the user settings are updated on any workstation that the user accesses. The specific Group Policy configuration will be found under User Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Folder Redirection. Folder redirection stores the common folders on a server so they follow the user to any workstation.
whyWrong: Login scripts are not used to configure folder redirection of the common user folders.
Organizational units can target users with settings but do not push out configuration settings themselves.
A home folder is one default folder assigned through a login script, not redirection of Desktop and Documents.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 11

stem: Which of the following is true about Active Directory security groups?
options: Security groups are used to assign permissions to shared resources
Security groups are used to organize user accounts
Security groups are used for email distribution lists
Security groups are used to control network connectivity
explanation: Active Directory security groups are primarily used to assign permissions to shared resources such as files, folders, printers, and other network resources. By assigning users or other groups to a security group, you can easily manage access control to various resources within the network.
whyWrong: Security groups can help organize accounts, but their main purpose is assigning access permissions.
Email distribution lists use distribution groups in Active Directory, not security groups.
Network connectivity is controlled with firewalls and network ACLs, not Active Directory security groups.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 13

stem: An administrator is creating an Active Directory (AD) organizational unit (OU) for the new research department. What is the primary purpose of an OU in Active Directory?
options: It determines the physical location of a user or computer object
It defines the security policies for a domain
It groups related objects for easier administration
It provides the domain name resolution services
explanation: An organizational unit (OU) is a container within an Active Directory domain that can be used to group related objects such as users, computers, and other OUs. The primary purpose of an OU is to organize and manage these objects in a logical hierarchy that reflects the organizational structure. An OU helps in applying group policies, permissions, and administrative tasks to a specific set of objects.
whyWrong: Physical location comes from attributes such as IP address or subnet, not from the OU an object is in.
Domain-wide security policies are set at the domain level; an OU groups objects for administration.
Name resolution is provided by the Domain Name System (DNS), not by organizational units.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 14

stem: An administrator is tasked with configuring permissions for the marketing folder on a user’s Windows 10 laptop. The permissions should allow the marketing team to have read permissions on the folder. What should the administrator configure to allow marketing users network access to the folder?
options: Set NTFS permissions to read for the marketing group
Choose to share the folder and give the marketing group read network access
Select the folder attributes and ensure read-only is checked
Set NTFS permissions to modify for the marketing group
explanation: Sharing the folder and giving the marketing group read network access will both set the local NTFS permission and also share the folder on the network. Without a share, the folder is not available to users across the network.
whyWrong: NTFS permissions alone do not share the folder, so users still cannot reach it over the network.
The read-only attribute only helps prevent accidental changes and does not share the folder.
Modify permissions grant more access than needed and still do not share the folder on the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.5 question 1

stem: A help desk receives a call from a home user who would like to synchronize their preferences, themes, and browser shortcuts when signing in to different Windows devices. Currently, the user has a unique local account configured on each device. The user would also prefer to have a single account for all devices. What feature would satisfy the user’s request?
options: Have the user create a Microsoft account and enable this on each device
Create a local account on the current device and copy the account to all devices
Have the user sign on with the default guest account on each device
Have the user sign in to the Edge browser and enable synchronization options
explanation: All the required settings will be saved with a Microsoft account that is centrally managed and available. This also supports single sign-on (SSO). The account can be enabled through the Windows settings menu.
whyWrong: A local account cannot be copied to other devices, and it does not synchronize settings.
The guest account is a poor security choice and is still only a local account.
Signing in to Edge only synchronizes browser settings and still needs a Microsoft account.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.5 question 2

stem: A standard user is assigned a second privileged account that can be used to reset other users’ passwords when requested. The user has access to the Active Directory Users and Computers (ADUC) console. What would be the recommended best security practice when considering the use of the two accounts? (Choose two.)
options: Always sign in to the workstation using a standard user account
Use the run as administrator option when using the privileged account
Always sign in to the workstation using the privileged user account
Use the run as standard user option when using the privileged account
explanation: Always signing in with a standard user account ensures that if the main user account is compromised, then an attacker will have limited privileges. Using run as administrator with the privileged account ensures the privileged account is exposed for short periods of time only.
whyWrong: Signing in with the privileged account all the time exposes high privileges if the session is compromised.
Running as a standard user would not give the rights needed to reset passwords in ADUC.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.5 question 3

stem: A user has requested to store sensitive information on a removable USB drive. Company policy states that all removable storage must support data encryption and all data must be encrypted at rest. What Windows feature can be used to meet the company policy?
explanation: BitLocker to Go is intended to protect removable media. The USB drive will be encrypted and will require a BitLocker password or smart card to be used to view any content on the drive.
whyWrong: PGP needs a third-party security suite and is not a built-in Windows feature.
The exFAT file system offers no built-in security or encryption features.
UAC prevents unauthorized configuration changes and does not encrypt removable drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.5 question 4

stem: A finance manager has raised a support ticket. They would like to protect sensitive files stored on Windows 10 workstations. The files contain customer details and are stored in a single folder. The files must be encrypted to meet security best practices. What can a support technician configure to protect the folder?
options: Enable Encrypting File System (EFS) for the folder
Enable BitLocker Drive Encryption for the folder
Enable BitLocker to Go on the folder
Ensure NTFS permissions are set to read for the finance team
explanation: EFS can enable a single file or an entire folder to be encrypted using AES symmetric encryption. The user who encrypts the folder will be the only user who will be able to decrypt the files contained within the folder. Additional users can be added at the owner’s discretion.
whyWrong: BitLocker Drive Encryption encrypts whole volumes and cannot be turned on for a single folder.
BitLocker to Go is only for removable media, not a folder on the workstation drive.
NTFS permissions control access but do not encrypt the data in the folder.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.5 question 5

stem: A technician is attempting to manually set an IP address on a server’s network interface card. They are prompted with a security dialog box, asking whether they approve of the application making changes to the computer. What has likely required this extra verification?
explanation: UAC is intended to prevent unauthorized configuration changes and will present the user with an option to use an administrator account or approve the action. Changing the IP address of a network card is a system change that triggers this prompt.
whyWrong: Defender Antivirus shows alerts about suspicious files, not prompts to approve configuration changes.
MFA asks for another factor at sign-in, not approval when changing a network card setting.
The change is to a network card, not to the firewall, so Defender Firewall does not prompt here.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.5 question 6

stem:
A recently installed database application has been configured and tested on a departmental server. The departmental users cannot connect to the application across the network. A technician performs a port scan on the server and observes the following output: Nmap scan report for 192.168.0.22 Host is up (0.000086s latency). Not shown: 994 closed ports PORT STATE SERVICE 135/tcp open msrpc 139/tcp open netbios-ssn 445/tcp open microsoft-ds 514/tcp open shell 3306/tcp filtered mysql

What should the technician do NEXT to allow users to access the database application?
options: Deactivate the Windows Defender firewall on the server
Activate the Windows Defender firewall on the users’ workstations
Add a firewall rule to allow inbound traffic to port 3306 on the server
Re-install the database application on the server and perform a system restart
explanation: When a firewall is blocking inbound connections to a port, then a scanner will show the port as being filtered. At the same time, we can see that the filtered port is associated with a database application (MySQL). A firewall rule that allows inbound traffic to port 3306 lets users reach the database.
whyWrong: Turning off the server firewall leaves the server unprotected from unwanted connections.
The block is on the server, so turning on firewalls on the workstations does not help.
Nothing shows the application is faulty, so reinstalling it will not open the filtered port.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.5 question 8

stem: Which network location type in Windows Defender Firewall offers the highest level of security?
explanation: The Public profile in Windows Firewall is the most restrictive. It is designed for use in public places where you have the least amount of trust in the network environment. It blocks many incoming connections and provides a higher level of security.
whyWrong: Home is a trusted network location that allows more incoming connections than Public.
Domain is a trusted network profile that does not block incoming connections as strictly as Public.
Work is not a valid Windows Defender Firewall profile.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.7 question 3
note: 220-1102 2.7; mapped to 220-1202 2.2 (Windows Firewall). Current Windows profiles are Domain, Private, and Public; Home and Work were older network location names.

stem: A manager shares a Reports folder from his desktop. Over the network, his assistant can open the reports but cannot save changes. The Sharing tab gives the assistant Full Control, and the Security tab gives her Read and Read & Execute. What is the MOST LIKELY reason she cannot save?
options: The NTFS permissions are more restrictive than the share permissions
The folder has the Hidden attribute set
The share name does not end with a dollar sign
The assistant's account is in the Guests group
explanation: When a user reaches a folder over the network, both share and NTFS permissions apply. The more restrictive of the two wins, so NTFS Read limits her to reading even with Full Control at the share. The manager must grant Modify or Write in the NTFS permissions.
whyWrong: The Hidden attribute only keeps a file out of normal folder listings; it does not block saving.
A dollar sign only hides a share from browsing and does not change what users can do in it.
Nothing points to the Guests group, and the permissions shown already explain the problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

stem: A sales director travels with a Windows 11 Pro laptop that has a TPM chip. If the laptop is stolen, nobody must be able to read anything on its internal SSD, even by moving the SSD to another computer. Which feature BEST meets this need?
explanation: BitLocker encrypts the whole internal volume and keeps its keys in the TPM. A drive moved to another computer stays unreadable without the key. It is included in Windows 11 Pro.
whyWrong: EFS encrypts chosen files and folders only, not the whole drive.
BitLocker To Go is meant for removable drives such as USB flash drives, not the internal SSD.
A PIN protects the sign-in but leaves the data on the drive unencrypted.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

stem: A school's IT technician wants the drives for each class's shared files to be mapped automatically whenever a teacher signs in to any domain computer. The drives are different for each department. What should the technician do BEST?
options: Assign a log-in script through a GPO linked to each department's OU
Set up a roaming profile for each teacher
Add each teacher to the Domain Admins group
Turn on BitLocker on each classroom computer
explanation: A log-in script runs tasks such as mapping network drives each time a user signs in to the domain. Linking it through a GPO to each department's OU lets each department get its own drives.
whyWrong: A roaming profile carries desktop settings between PCs but does not map department drives on its own.
Domain Admins gets full control of the domain, which breaks least privilege and maps no drives.
BitLocker encrypts drives at rest and has nothing to do with mapping network shares.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

stem: Which encryption protocol is deprecated?
explanation: WEP is a deprecated wireless encryption technology. WEP keys can be cracked in minutes, so WPA2 or WPA3 should be used instead.
whyWrong: WAP stands for wireless access point, a device, not an encryption protocol.
WPA2 is still in use and supported for wireless security.
WPA3 is the current and most secure wireless security protocol.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 20: Wireless Networking, Chapter Review question 2

stem: What is the primary purpose of Kerberos?
options: To provide centralized administration for dial-up, VPN, and wireless authentication
To act as a three-headed guard dog protecting network servers from illegitimate login attempts
To enable computers to securely prove their identity to each other in client/server environments
To separate authentication, authorization, and accounting functions for network access
explanation: To enable computers to securely prove their identity to each other in client/server environments, especially with Active Directory, is the primary purpose of Kerberos. Kerberos uses tickets from a trusted server, so passwords are not sent across the network.
whyWrong: Centralized administration for dial-up, VPN, and wireless authentication is the job of RADIUS.
Kerberos is named after a three-headed dog, but its purpose is authentication, not guarding servers.
Separating authentication, authorization, and accounting is a feature of TACACS+.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 35
note: Kerberos is listed under 220-1202 2.3 (authentication); the classification gave 2.1.

stem: You have been tasked with setting up a SOHO wireless network in a small healthcare office that cannot afford a server. The wireless users require the highest level of security available, and various other levels of desktop authentication for access to cloud-based resources. Which of the following protocols and authentication methods should you implement? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: For the highest level of wireless security, use WPA3 (and AES). For authentication, select multifactor authentication (MFA). Many healthcare providers are required to log on with a username/password and a smart card (or biometric).
whyWrong: WPA is outdated and much weaker than WPA3.
WPA2 is still used, but WPA3 is the highest level of wireless security.
TKIP is an outdated encryption protocol with known weaknesses.
RADIUS needs an authentication server, which the office cannot afford.
TACACS+ needs an authentication server, which the office cannot afford.
SSO may already exist in the cloud, but it is not the authentication method to set up at this office.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 46

stem: A technician is asked to re-deploy unused wireless access points for the new warehouse. The devices have been in storage since 2015. The technician must ensure they are configured with the most secure wireless network settings. Bearing in mind the age of the equipment, which configuration will provide the technician with the most secure implementation?
explanation: Given the age of the equipment, the most secure option for the wireless network would be WPA2 with AES encryption. WPA2 provides robust security measures, and Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is a widely accepted and secure encryption algorithm for wireless communication. Although WPA3 and AES-256 or AES-128 are more recent advancements, they might not be supported by older wireless equipment. WPA2 was released in 2004, and WPA3 in 2018.
whyWrong: WPA3 with AES-128 is stronger, but devices from 2015 are not likely to support WPA3.
WPA3 with AES-256 is the strongest, but devices from 2015 are not likely to support WPA3.
TKIP is an old encryption method with known weaknesses.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 6
note: 220-1102 2.2; mapped to 220-1202 2.3 (protocols and encryption). The book's explanation said 2013; the stem says 2015, so the dates in the explanation were adjusted.

stem: The service desk for a large financial institution has raised support tickets after several members of staff returned to the workplace, after months of working remotely from home. When the users attempt to connect to the wired network, they encounter login errors. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of the login issue for the users, considering that the network uses 802.1X with EAP-TLS for wired network authentication?
options: The OS may need the latest security updates
An important service has not started
The client certificates may have expired
explanation: The user’s inability to log in to the network after an extended period of absence, with the network utilizing 802.1X and EAP-TLS for authentication on the wired network, can be attributed to various factors. However, the most probable cause in this scenario is an expired certificate. Since the user has been away for several months, it is possible that the certificate used for authentication has expired during that period, leading to the login issue.
whyWrong: Missing updates do not stop 802.1X certificate authentication.
A stopped service is not the likely cause after months away with certificate-based logins.
An application crash does not cause a network login error.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 9

stem: A technician has been tasked with configuring a new wireless router for the payroll office. They must ensure optimal security is configured. Which of the following security measures should the technician implement to achieve the highest level of wireless network protection?
explanation: To achieve the highest level of wireless network security, the technician should implement WPA3. WPA3 is the latest security protocol, and it provides strong encryption algorithms and enhanced protection against unauthorized access. It offers improved security features compared to its predecessors, such as WPA2 and WEP.
whyWrong: WPS has known weaknesses and should be disabled.
TKIP is an old protocol that is less secure than WPA3.
WEP is outdated and easily broken.
MAC filtering can be bypassed and is not enough on its own.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 55
note: 220-1102 2.2; mapped to 220-1202 2.3 (wireless security protocols and authentication).

stem: A large online retailer must support wireless networks in all of its main warehouse facilities, where there is a mixture of older wireless access points using WPA2 and newer equipment supporting WPA3. Which of the following is an advantage of continuing to support WPA2 instead of WPA3?
explanation: WPA2 offers an advantage over WPA3 in terms of greater backward compatibility. WPA2 has been widely adopted and implemented in a vast array of devices, including older ones. When upgrading to WPA3, some older devices might not support the newer protocol, leading to connectivity issues. Therefore, opting for WPA2 can ensure that a wider range of devices can still connect securely to the network.
whyWrong: WPA3 is more secure than WPA2.
WPA3 has better resistance to brute-force attacks through SAE.
Support for larger networks is not an advantage of WPA2 over WPA3.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 82
note: 220-1102 2.2; mapped to 220-1202 2.3 (wireless security protocols and authentication).

stem: You are setting up a new wireless network for a small office. Which wireless encryption method provides the highest level of security?
explanation: WPA2 is the most secure option listed here. It provides strong encryption and is recommended for securing wireless networks. WPA3 would be stronger still, but it is not one of the options here.
whyWrong: WEP is outdated and insecure.
WPA is better than WEP but weaker than WPA2.
WPS is a setup convenience feature, not an encryption method.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 84

stem: What of the following is the most secure wireless encryption standard for 802.11 networks?
explanation: WEP was the original encryption standard developed for Wi-Fi networks, but it is easily hacked. WPA is an upgrade, but WPA2 is more secure and incorporates the entire 802.11i standard. WPA3 is of course the safest.
whyWrong: WEP was the original Wi-Fi encryption standard and is easily cracked.
WPA improved on WEP but still relies on TKIP, which is now considered weak.
WPA2 is strong, but WPA3 adds newer protections such as SAE and is the most secure.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 4
note: From a Core 1 chapter; wireless security protocols are 220-1202 2.3.

stem: Which of the following security standards was the first to introduce a dynamic 128-bit per-packet security key?
explanation: WEP could use a 64-bit or 128-bit security key, but it was a static key. TKIP introduced a dynamic per-packet key. AES and CCMP came after TKIP.
whyWrong: WEP used a 64-bit or 128-bit key, but the key was static, not per packet.
AES is a block cipher that came after TKIP and is used by WPA2 and WPA3.
CCMP is the AES-based protocol of WPA2, which came after TKIP.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 14
note: From a Core 1 chapter; TKIP is a 220-1202 2.3 topic.

stem: You have set up a wireless router on your network and configured it to use AES. What configuration option do you need to choose on the client computers?
explanation: If your router is using AES, the clients will need to use WPA2 or WPA3. TKIP is a protocol utilized by WPA. WEP is the weakest of the encryption options.
whyWrong: WEP uses the RC4 cipher, not AES, and is the weakest option.
WPA normally uses TKIP; AES became required with WPA2.
TKIP is the encryption protocol of WPA, not AES.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 18
note: From a Core 1 chapter; wireless security protocols are 220-1202 2.3.

stem: Which wireless encryption protocol provides Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) encryption?
explanation: Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) offers the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) for encrypting wireless communications. Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) offers weak 64- or 128-bit encryption. Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) uses the RC4 encryption algorithm. Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) is a part of the WPA encryption protocol.
whyWrong: WEP uses weak RC4 encryption with 64- or 128-bit keys, not AES.
The original WPA uses RC4 with TKIP, not AES.
TKIP is the key protocol of WPA that is built on RC4, not AES.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 10

stem: Which of the following is the strongest form of wireless encryption?
explanation: Of the list of options, Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is the strongest form of wireless encryption. WPA is a wireless encryption protocol, but it is deprecated; WPA2 or WPA3 is recommended. TKIP is deprecated and has been compromised; it should be avoided.
whyWrong: WPA3 is a wireless security protocol that uses AES; the encryption itself is AES.
WPA is a deprecated wireless security protocol; WPA2 or WPA3 is recommended instead.
TKIP is deprecated and has been compromised, so it should be avoided.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware, Cram Quiz 1 question 1

stem: You have been tasked with connecting wireless clients to a server that supports SSO and 802.1X. Which of the following technologies should you implement? (Select the two BEST answers.)
explanation: To take advantage of single sign-on (SSO) and 802.1X, you would need a special authentication system (such as RADIUS) on the server side and WPA2-Enterprise on the client side (sometimes abbreviated as WPA2-ENT). WPA2-PSK uses a preshared key that is stored on the AP, and it doesn’t support the other technologies. WEP and TKIP are outdated and should be avoided. Kerberos is a mutual authentication protocol used by Active Directory and other directory services programs.
whyWrong: WPA2-PSK uses a preshared key stored on the AP and does not use 802.1X or an authentication server.
WEP is an outdated, broken protocol that does not support 802.1X enterprise authentication.
TKIP is an outdated encryption protocol and does not provide 802.1X authentication.
Kerberos is the mutual authentication protocol of Active Directory, not the 802.1X server for wireless clients.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware, Cram Quiz 1 question 2
note: The book's explanation also asks which port RADIUS uses by default; RADIUS uses UDP 1812 for authentication and 1813 for accounting.

stem: What is the primary advantage of TACACS+ over RADIUS for authentication?
options: TACACS+ uses UDP, which is considered more reliable than TCP used by RADIUS.
TACACS+ combines authentication and authorization for greater efficiency.
TACACS+ separates authentication and authorization, providing an additional layer of security.
TACACS+ operates on ports 1812 and 1813, which are more secure than the port used by RADIUS.
explanation: TACACS+ enhances security by separating authentication and authorization into distinct operations, unlike RADIUS, which combines them. This separation allows for more granular control and can prevent unauthorized access even if one factor is compromised. TACACS+ actually uses TCP, which is generally considered more reliable than UDP used by RADIUS, so that answer is just wrong. Also, RADIUS combines authentication and authorization, whereas TACACS+ separates them. TACACS+ uses port 49, whereas RADIUS uses ports 1812 and 1813.
whyWrong: TACACS+ uses TCP, not UDP, and RADIUS uses UDP, so this option has the protocols reversed.
RADIUS combines authentication and authorization; TACACS+ separates them.
TACACS+ uses port 49; ports 1812 and 1813 belong to RADIUS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware, Cram Quiz 1 question 3

stem: Which of the following wireless encryption protocols offers 256-bit encryption?
explanation: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) can be used with WPA2 and WPA3. It is the encryption algorithm used by US government agencies and can offer up to 256-bit encryption! TKIP is an old encryption protocol used with WEP and WPA and should not be used anymore. Normally, WPA2 uses standard 128-bit AES encryption, but you can configure it to use 256-bit AES encryption. So, yes, WPA2 and WPA3 can use 256-bit AES encryption, but it’s AES itself that can do 256-bit encryption.
whyWrong: TKIP is an old encryption protocol used with WEP and WPA and does not offer 256-bit encryption.
WPA2 normally uses 128-bit AES; any 256-bit encryption comes from AES itself.
WPA3 uses 128-bit or 192-bit AES by default; the 256-bit strength comes from AES itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware, Cram Quiz 1 question 4

stem: A security consultant is advising a small business on the subject of securing the Wi-Fi network when giving access to customers. The small business only has access to a wireless router provided by the internet service provider (ISP). The business intends to print a code on the bottom of till receipts to allow customers to access the Wi-Fi. Which wireless standard offers the highest levels of security when a customer needs to access the Wi-Fi using a supplied passcode/passkey?
explanation: Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 (WPA3) uses a secure handshaking process called simultaneous authentication of equals (SAE). This replaces the previous method, called preshared key (PSK), so a shared passcode is much harder to attack.
whyWrong: WPA2 uses the older preshared key handshake, which is weaker than the SAE handshake of WPA3.
TKIP is an older encryption protocol made for WPA with RC4, not the most secure current standard.
AES is an encryption cipher used inside WPA2 and WPA3, not a wireless security standard on its own.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.2 question 1

stem: A security team is planning for the deployment of Wi-Fi for internal business units. It is anticipated that over 50% of the workforce will need secure access to Wi-Fi. Management is insisting that all users should use unique domain credentials to authenticate onto the network. What service can be deployed to ensure user authentication requests are securely passed back to the Active Directory?
explanation: Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) is also referred to as an authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA) service. RADIUS servers allow the Wi-Fi controller to forward authentication requests from client devices. These authentication requests will then be forwarded to directory services.
whyWrong: WPS pairs a device with a router without typing a key; it does not use domain credentials.
An open WEP network needs no account or password, so it cannot check domain credentials.
WPA-PSK uses one shared key for everyone and does not pass requests to Active Directory.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.2 question 2

stem: A technician is configuring a wireless LAN and must ensure that the configuration of the Wi-Fi router supports the latest encryption standards. What configuration choice would BEST protect confidential data sent over Wi-Fi?
explanation: WPA2-AES offers the highest levels of security of these choices. It uses AES 128-bit encryption.
whyWrong: WEP is over 20 years old, is no longer used, and is not secure.
WPA2-TKIP uses the older RC4 encryption algorithm, which is weaker than AES.
Open Wi-Fi networks do not use any encryption at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.2 question 3

stem: Zander downloaded a game off the Internet and installed it, but as soon as he started to play, he got a Blue Screen of Death. Upon rebooting, he discovered that his Documents folder had been erased. What happened?
options: He broke the Local Security Policy.
explanation: Zander clearly installed a Trojan, a virus masquerading as a game. A Trojan hides inside a program that looks useful, so the user installs it willingly.
whyWrong: Spyware hides and collects information; it does not usually erase files.
Group Policy is a set of configuration rules; it cannot be broken by installing a game.
The Local Security Policy is a set of settings; installing a game does not break it.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 27: Securing Computers, Chapter Review question 5

stem: Malware that encrypts a hard drive and demands payment in exchange for decryption is known as what?
explanation: Malware that demands money in exchange for hard drive decryption is called ransomware. Good offline backups are the best protection, because the files can be restored without paying.
whyWrong: A Trojan hides inside a program that looks useful; encryption for payment is ransomware.
A cryptominer uses the computer's resources to mine currency; it does not hold files for ransom.
A keylogger records keystrokes; it does not encrypt the drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 27: Securing Computers, Chapter Review question 7

stem: Which of the following technologies focuses on analyzing endpoint activity to detect unexpected behavior and potential threats, providing context for incident response?
explanation: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) agents continuously monitor endpoint activity, collecting detailed telemetry like process executions, network connections, and file modifications. This data is analyzed to detect unexpected behavior and potential threats, providing security analysts with context for incident response.
whyWrong: An EPP mainly blocks known and zero-day malware; it is not mainly about analyzing activity.
MDR is a managed service built on top of EDR data, not the detection technology itself.
An email security gateway checks email traffic, not endpoint activity.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 11

stem: A service desk technician is responding to a service ticket that appears to indicate the presence of a rootkit. In order to resolve the suspected rootkit installation, which of the following options would be the MOST effective?
explanation: The most effective solution for dealing with a suspected rootkit is to utilize anti-malware software. Rootkits are sophisticated types of malware that can deeply embed themselves within the operating system, making them difficult to detect and remove. Anti-malware software is specifically designed to identify and eliminate such threats, providing the best chance of successfully removing the rootkit from the system.
whyWrong: Updating applications patches flaws but does not remove a rootkit.
Reinstalling the OS is a drastic step for when other methods fail.
Restoring files may recover data but does not remove the rootkit.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 5

stem: A customer services representative asks a professional to fix a laptop problem. The representative complains that the browser redirects to several pages and programs open without being activated. Which of the following is the MOST LIKELY cause?
explanation: Based on the symptoms described by the user, the most likely cause of the issue is a virus. Viruses are malicious software programs that can replicate and spread, causing various disruptions to the normal functioning of a computer system. In this case, the unauthorized opening of applications and browser redirects are common signs of a virus infection.
whyWrong: A keylogger records keystrokes; it does not redirect the browser or open programs.
Cryptominers slow the computer but do not usually redirect the browser.
Malware is the general category, while virus is the more exact answer the book wants.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 57

stem: Upon investigating, a technician uncovers that user input has been surreptitiously captured by a malicious actor. Considering the circumstances, which of the following malware types is the MOST probable cause for this occurrence?
explanation: In this scenario, the most likely malware type being used is a keylogger. Keyloggers are designed to clandestinely record keystrokes made by users, capturing sensitive information such as passwords, credit card details, and other confidential data. By surreptitiously logging user input, keyloggers enable malicious actors to obtain unauthorized access to valuable information.
whyWrong: Cryptominers use computing power to mine currency, not to capture input.
A rootkit hides and gives control but is not mainly for capturing input.
Spear phishing is a targeted social engineering attack, not malware that records input.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 71

stem: Which of the following is different from a virus in that it can reproduce itself, is self-contained, and doesn't need a host application to be transported?
explanation: A worm is different from a virus in that it can reproduce itself, is self-contained, and doesn't need a host application to be transported. A smurf attack is a type of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS). A phishing attack is an attempt to gain a user's credentials to a network resource. Trojan horses are programs that enter a system or network under the guise of another program.
whyWrong: A Smurf attack is a denial-of-service flood, not self-copying malware.
Phishing is a social engineering attempt to steal credentials, not self-copying malware.
A Trojan hides inside a legitimate-looking program and does not copy itself on its own.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 10

stem: You need to protect your users from potentially being phished via email. Which of the following should you use to protect them?
explanation: End-user education is the best way to protect your users from the threat of phishing via email. Antivirus software is used to prevent viruses, not phishing attempts. SecureDNS can be useful in protecting your users, but not from phishing emails. The principle of least privilege assigns only the permissions that users need to do their work, and no more. Trained users learn to recognize a suspicious email and report it instead of clicking its links.
whyWrong: Antivirus software stops viruses, but phishing emails trick the user rather than run code.
Secure DNS can block some bad sites but does not stop users from answering phishing emails.
Least privilege limits what an account can do; it does not teach users to spot phishing.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 14

stem: Internal users suspect there have been repeated attempts to infect their systems, as reported to them by pop-up messages from their antivirus software. According to the messages, the virus seems to be the same in every case. What is the MOST LIKELY culprit?
options: A server is acting as a carrier for a virus.
A password attack is being carried out.
A DoS attack is under way.
explanation: Some viruses won't damage a system in an attempt to spread into all the other systems in a network. These viruses use that system as the carrier of the virus. A password attack would not prompt your antivirus software to notify you. Your antivirus software could be malfunctioning, but it would not suggest the same virus is infecting you over and over again. A denial-of-service (DoS) attack would not prompt your antivirus to notify you.
whyWrong: A password attack would not cause antivirus pop-ups about the same virus.
A malfunctioning antivirus would not keep reporting the same virus from repeated infection attempts.
A denial-of-service attack floods services and would not trigger repeated virus alerts.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 16

stem: You're working late one night and notice that the hard drive on your new computer is very active even though you aren't doing anything on the computer and it isn't connected to the Internet. What is the MOST LIKELY suspect?
options: A spear phishing attack is being performed.
A virus is spreading in your system.
Your system is under a DoS attack.
explanation: A symptom of many viruses is unusual activity on the system disk. The virus spreading to other files on your system causes this. A disk failure will not create high disk activity. A spear phishing attack is a social engineering attack and will not create high disk activity; neither denial-of-service attacks nor TCP/IP hijacking attacks will create high disk activity.
whyWrong: Spear phishing is a targeted social engineering email and does not cause disk activity on an idle offline system.
A denial-of-service attack comes over the network, and this computer is not connected to the Internet.
TCP/IP hijacking needs a network connection, and it does not cause heavy disk activity.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 17

stem: Your boss needs you to present to upper management the need for a firewall for the network. What is the thesis of your presentation?
options: The isolation of one network from another
The scanning of all packets for viruses
explanation: The thesis of your presentation should outline the need of a firewall to isolate the external network from the internal network. Firewalls will not scan packets for viruses. Firewalls will not prevent password attacks or harden physical security.
whyWrong: Firewalls filter traffic by rules; scanning packets for viruses is the job of antivirus software.
A firewall does not stop password guessing against an allowed service.
A firewall is a logical network control, not a physical security measure.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 19

stem: Which of the following types of malware is designed to gain administrative-level control of a system?
explanation: A rootkit is designed to get administrative control of a computer system. The word root is synonymous with administrator in some systems (such as Linux and UNIX). Ransomware is malware that encrypts a person’s files so that they are not accessible. Keyloggers capture the keystrokes a person makes on a keyboard. Spyware is malware that is used to watch (and possibly record) what a person is doing on a system and on the Internet.
whyWrong: Ransomware encrypts a person's files and demands payment; it is not defined by gaining admin control.
A keylogger captures keystrokes to steal passwords; it is not designed to gain administrative control.
Spyware watches and records what a person does; it is not designed to gain administrative control.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware, Cram Quiz 2 question 1

stem: You have been tasked with implementing a virus prevention plan on a group of Windows client computers. Which of the following should you carry out? (Select all that apply.)
options: Verify that a firewall is installed.
explanation: First of all, update everything. Then verify that antimalware software and a firewall are installed and updated. Be sure to update the OS and apps as well. Microsoft 365 is especially susceptible to malware, so if you run it, you have to keep a close eye on it. Configuring File History or any other backup methods won’t prevent malware from occurring, but it is important to do this nonetheless.
whyWrong: File History backs up files; a backup helps recovery but does not prevent malware.
A rootkit scanner may find rootkits, but it does not scan for viruses or prevent them.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware, Cram Quiz 2 question 2

stem: One of your customers complains of a problem: When browsing the Internet, multiple browser pages start opening automatically. You notice that the computer is performing poorly, even when not connected to the Internet. What should you do?
explanation: Chances are that the customer’s computer does not have an antivirus or antimalware program running. Install one (or enable one if it already exists). However, the problem is probably worse than that, and the system likely needs to be remediated (isolated, scanned, and so on). These are probably not just pop-ups; you normally see only one legitimate pop-up at a time. Plus, the computer is performing poorly, even when not connected to the Internet.
whyWrong: A pop-up blocker does not help here, because the poor performance offline shows that malware is the cause.
Rebooting can fix some issues, but it does not remove malware from an infected system.
Updating definitions does not help if no antimalware program is running, and the cause may not be a virus.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware, Cram Quiz 2 question 3

stem: Which security solution focuses on unifying security data from various sources, including endpoints, networks, cloud workloads, and email, into a centralized platform for a holistic and proactive security approach?
explanation: XDR is the only solution that collects and correlates security data from various sources beyond just endpoints. It provides a centralized platform for a more comprehensive and proactive security approach. EPP focuses on preventing known and zero-day malware from executing on endpoints. EDR monitors endpoint activity and collects telemetry data for analysis and threat detection. MDR augments EDR with 24/7 monitoring and incident response by security experts.
whyWrong: EPP stops known and zero-day malware from running on endpoints only; it does not unify other data sources.
EDR monitors and collects telemetry from endpoints only, not from networks, cloud workloads, and email.
MDR adds round-the-clock expert monitoring and response to EDR; it is a service, not a unified data platform.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware, Cram Quiz 2 question 4

stem: Which Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) mode would be most suitable for a user who wants to undo recent software installations that have caused the system to become unstable?
explanation: System Restore allows users to revert their system to a previous state, effectively undoing any recent changes that may have caused instability or errors. In this scenario, where software installations have led to instability, using System Restore to roll back the system to a point before the installations would be the most appropriate solution. Startup Repair mode is designed to fix common startup problems, such as missing or corrupted system files, but it may not address issues caused by software installations. Command Prompt mode provides a command-line interface for manual troubleshooting, but it requires advanced knowledge and may not be the most efficient solution for this scenario. System Image Recovery mode restores the entire system from a backup, which is a more drastic measure than necessary for addressing instability caused by software installations!
whyWrong: Startup Repair fixes common startup problems such as missing boot files, not unwanted software installations.
Command Prompt needs advanced knowledge for manual repairs and is not the simplest way to undo installations.
System Image Recovery restores the whole system from a backup, which is more drastic than needed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware, Cram Quiz 2 question 5
note: WinRE recovery options are listed under 220-1202 2.4 tools and methods (Recovery Console); the scenario also fits 3.1.

stem: Which term describes software, such as an extra toolbar, that comes bundled with a legitimate free program and that the user did not mean to install?
explanation: A potentially unwanted program is software the user did not intend to install, often bundled with a free download. Examples include adware, browser toolbars, and other extra utilities that ride along in the installer. PUPs are not always harmful, but they can slow the system and collect data.
whyWrong: A rootkit hides deep in the OS to give an attacker hidden control, not a bundled toolbar.
A boot sector virus infects the boot code of a drive and is not offered as an optional install.
A keylogger secretly records keystrokes and is not a visible bundled toolbar or utility.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 5: Security Concepts

stem: A user downloads a free video converter and clicks through its installer with the default choices. Since then, banner ads and pop-ups appear even when no browser is open, and the laptop feels slower. What is the MOST LIKELY cause?
options: Adware that was bundled with the free program
Ransomware that has encrypted the user's files
A boot sector virus in the drive's startup code
A failing hard drive with bad sectors
explanation: Adware delivers unwanted ads such as pop-ups and banners and is often bundled with free software. Accepting the default install options is a common way it gets installed. The extra processes that show the ads also use resources, which explains the slowdown.
whyWrong: Ransomware locks or encrypts files and demands payment; it does not show advertising banners.
A boot sector virus affects startup and would not show advertising pop-ups after a software install.
A failing drive can cause slowness and errors, but it does not make ads appear.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 5: Security Concepts

stem: Which TWO practices help users avoid installing adware and other PUPs along with free software? (Choose two.)
options: Read each installer screen before clicking to continue
Choose the custom installation option and clear the extra components
Use the express or default installation to save time
Turn off User Account Control before installing
explanation: Adware and PUPs often ride along in the installers of free programs. Reading each prompt shows the offers for extra toolbars or utilities. The custom installation option lets the user clear those extras before they are installed.
whyWrong: The express or default install usually accepts every bundled offer, which is how PUPs get installed.
Turning off UAC removes a warning prompt and makes it easier, not harder, for unwanted software to install.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 5: Security Concepts

stem: What do boot sector viruses target?
options: Files stored on external hard drives
The master boot record or boot sector of a computer
explanation: Boot sector viruses infect the master boot record (MBR) or the boot sector of a computer system’s hard drive. When the infected computer starts up, the virus becomes active and can spread to other parts of the system.
whyWrong: A boot sector virus targets the drive that boots the OS, not files on external storage.
Network routers and switches are not targeted by boot sector viruses.
Stealing passwords and login credentials is linked to keyloggers, social engineering, or password attacks.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 1

stem: What is the primary purpose of a keylogger?
options: To delete files and disrupt system operations
To track user activities and collect sensitive information
To capture and record keystrokes on a computer
explanation: Keyloggers are able to record every keystroke made by a user on a targeted system. Attackers use it to steal login credentials, sensitive information, and payment card numbers.
whyWrong: Mining cryptocurrency is what a cryptominer does, not a keylogger.
Deleting files and disrupting systems describes destructive malware such as viruses, not a keylogger.
Tracking user activity in general describes spyware; a keylogger specifically records keystrokes.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 2

stem: What are the typical signs that a ransomware attack is taking place?
options: An attacker is exploiting software vulnerabilities
An attacker is tracking user activities and collecting sensitive information
An attacker is encrypting files and demanding a ransom for their release
An attacker is hijacking a computer’s boot process
explanation: Ransomware is malware that encrypts a victim’s data files, making them inaccessible. This is then followed by a demand for payment in order to receive the decryption key.
whyWrong: Exploiting software vulnerabilities is a general attack method, not the sign of a ransomware attack.
Tracking user activities and collecting information describes spyware, not ransomware.
Hijacking the boot process describes a boot sector virus or rootkit, not ransomware.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 3

stem: Technicians are investigating an issue with a sales department laptop computer. Windows Defender Security features are turned off and when the technicians attempt to re-enable the features, the settings are reversed. What type of malware may be the cause of the issue?
explanation: A rootkit will replace a privileged OS executable and is then able to block and disrupt OS processes. When a privileged account is used to configure OS functions or services, the rootkit can override these actions.
whyWrong: A trojan hides inside useful software and does not usually keep reversing security settings.
A virus focuses on replicating and spreading rather than repeatedly undoing Defender settings.
Spyware may weaken security, but its main goal is collecting data, not overriding OS settings.
Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment instead of quietly reversing security settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 4

stem: Security staff are preparing a set of automated actions to assist the service desk when dealing with malware incidents. They propose to create a number of playbooks to assist the team. One scenario requires the entire hard drive to be erased and the OS to be re-installed. What malware type would require this action?
explanation: Rootkits are difficult to remove as they will replace key system files and block attempts to remove malicious files. Completely wiping or erasing the hard drive will ensure no malicious files remain.
whyWrong: An up-to-date anti-malware suite can usually remove a trojan without wiping the drive.
A virus can normally be detected and removed by anti-malware without reinstalling the OS.
Spyware can usually be removed with anti-malware tools, so a full wipe is not needed.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 5

stem: A user calls the service desk, complaining that after opening a file sent by a co-worker, they can no longer access any local folders. In addition, they see pop-up messages displaying a telephone number and requests to make payments to fix the problem. What has likely caused this issue on the user’s computer?
explanation: Ransomware demands a payment be made to access the data. Ransomware typically forces the user or organization to make a payment as important personal or business data has been encrypted by the attacker.
whyWrong: A trojan hides inside a useful application and does not normally lock folders and demand payment.
A rootkit replaces privileged OS files to hide and disrupt processes, not to demand a ransom.
A virus spreads through files and attachments but does not usually block data and ask for payment.
Spyware runs quietly in the background to steal information and avoids showing any messages.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 6

stem: After installing a number of technical preventative controls on the company network, in order to reduce malware incidents, there has been a 90% reduction in infected systems. The controls consist of spam filters, content inspection, and endpoint detection and response (EDR). In addition to these technical controls, what would be most effective in further reducing malware incidents?
explanation: As there is no specific malware type mentioned, the best approach is to roll out user awareness training to cover a broad range of threats. Training on common threats adds a human control to the technical controls already in place.
whyWrong: Training about rootkits alone covers only one malware type, not the broad range of threats.
Training about viruses alone covers only one malware type and leaves other threats unaddressed.
Training about spyware alone covers a single threat type instead of common threats in general.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 7
note: 220-1102 2.3; mapped to 220-1202 2.4 (user education regarding common threats).

stem: A user calls the service desk after receiving a number of messages in the Windows 10 action center. The messages appear to be non-malicious and are being generated by the web browser. What action would be the BEST to remediate this issue?
options: Block all outgoing traffic on ports 80 and 443
explanation: As the web browser is the source of the incident and has access to websites, it makes sense to ensure the activity is not malicious. If the activity is harmless, then the anti-virus scan can confirm this.
whyWrong: Disabling the web browser is very disruptive and does not find out whether the messages are harmful.
Blocking ports 80 and 443 stops all web traffic, which is far too disruptive for this issue.
Reinstalling the OS is very disruptive and should be used only as a last resort.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 8

stem: A recent spate of spam emails has targeted the finance team. The emails appear to originate from genuine suppliers and often contain links to reset login details. What course of action will BEST help to reduce these incidents?
explanation: Links sent in email messages are phishing attacks. In this case, specific training to counter this type of attack is the best solution.
whyWrong: A software firewall does not block links and content embedded in an email message.
General training on common threats is less effective here than training aimed at phishing.
Reinstalling the OS does not help because no operating system has been compromised.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 9

stem: A company has recently seen a high number of user accounts compromised. The accounts belong to the engineering team, which hot desks using a limited number of engineering workstations. Despite the user passwords being reset, the problem persists. What is the MOST LIKELY reason for the accounts being compromised?
options: Hardware keyloggers on the engineering workstations
explanation: As the compromised accounts are associated with a specific number of workstations, the hardware could have been the vector of attack. As the accounts have had passwords reset, this would not be effective as the keylogger will reveal the new passwords.
whyWrong: A remote access trojan gives control of a system, but it does not explain why only shared desks are affected.
A rootkit intercepts calls to system services and is not the most likely cause tied to these desks.
Cryptominers use CPU and GPU cycles to mine currency and do not steal user credentials.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 11

stem: A number of users recently returned from a marketing event with digital promotional materials provided on USB media. The service desk received a number of calls from the users complaining that applications are slow to load and their workstations are unacceptably slow. After investigation, it appears that CPU/GPU activity is running at 100%. What type of malware is MOST LIKELY affecting the users?
explanation: Malicious cryptominers may be downloaded using a web browser or as a mobile app. The software will steal the resources of the computer to generate new cryptocurrency. This will target the central processing unit (CPU) and the graphical processing unit (GPU) found on advanced graphics cards.
whyWrong: Spyware gathers private information and may slow a system, but it does not drive the CPU and GPU to 100%.
Keyloggers record keystrokes to a log file and do not use large amounts of CPU and GPU time.
A boot sector virus replaces boot files to load at startup and does not keep the processors at full load.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.3 question 12

stem: What is the process for using or manipulating people to gain access to network resources?
explanation: Social engineering is the process of using or manipulating people to gain access to network resources. Phishing, tailgating, and impersonation are common examples of social engineering.
whyWrong: Cracking is breaking passwords or encryption, not manipulating people.
Hacking is a general term for gaining unauthorized access, not specifically through people.
Network engineering is the design and building of networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 27: Securing Computers, Chapter Review question 1
note: 220-1102 2.4; mapped to 220-1202 2.5 (social engineering, threats, and vulnerabilities).

stem: John dressed up in a fake security guard uniform matching the ones used by a company and then walked into the company’s headquarters with some legitimate employees in an attempt to gain access to company resources. What kind of attack is this?
explanation: John just practiced tailgating on the unsuspecting company. The fake uniform adds impersonation, but following employees through the door is tailgating.
whyWrong: Administrative access is a level of privilege, not a way of getting into a building.
Data destruction is the removal of data, not an attack on building access.
Spoofing fakes an address or identity on a network; walking in with employees is tailgating.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 27: Securing Computers, Chapter Review question 8

stem: Andre, CEO of a midsized company, received an e-mail that appeared to be from a colleague that wanted to close a major deal. Suspicious because the deal in question didn’t exist, he called in his IT security team who determined that it came from a spoofed IP address. Which of the following BEST describes this attempted attack?
explanation: Andre was the target of a whaling attempt. Whaling is phishing aimed at a high-value target such as an executive.
whyWrong: Phishing is broad, while an attack aimed at a CEO has a more exact name.
A zero-day attack uses an unknown software flaw, not a deceptive email.
Tailgating is following someone through a secure door, not sending an email.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 27: Securing Computers, Chapter Review question 9

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the primary tactic used in a business email compromise (BEC) attack?
options: Exploiting vulnerabilities in third-party software to infiltrate a target's network
Inserting malicious scripts into a web page to gain elevated privileges
Impersonating trusted individuals via email to deceive employees into transferring funds or divulging information
Injecting malicious code into the software build or update process
explanation: Impersonating trusted individuals via email to deceive employees into transferring funds or divulging information. Business email compromise (BEC) is a sophisticated scam where attackers impersonate trusted individuals, like executives or vendors, via email to trick employees into transferring funds or divulging sensitive information.
whyWrong: Exploiting third-party software to reach a target describes a supply chain attack.
Inserting malicious scripts into a web page describes cross-site scripting.
Injecting code into a software build or update describes a pipeline attack.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 6

stem: A company employee receives a phone call from an individual falsely claiming to represent a mortgage company. Which of the following BEST describes this incident?
explanation: The incident described in the question is an example of impersonation. Impersonation occurs when someone fraudulently pretends to be another person or entity in order to deceive others. In this case, the caller is posing as a representative of a mortgage company, attempting to gain the trust of the company employee and potentially deceive them into revealing sensitive information or performing unauthorized actions. As the exploit involves the placing of a phone call, this could also be termed a Vishing exploit.
whyWrong: Social engineering is the broad category; impersonation describes this call more exactly.
Phishing usually uses email or websites, not a phone call.
Identity theft is using stolen personal information, which this call does not describe.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 27
note: 220-1102 2.4; mapped to 220-1202 2.5 (social engineering, threats, and vulnerabilities).

stem: During a hotel stay, a guest wants to connect to the hotel Wi-Fi network but notices that several SSIDs have extremely similar names. What social engineering attack is MOST LIKELY being attempted in this scenario?
explanation: In an evil twin attack, an attacker sets up a rogue Wi-Fi access point that mimics a legitimate network, often using a similar or identical SSID. The intention is to deceive users into connecting to the malicious network, enabling the attacker to intercept sensitive information or perform other malicious activities. It is important for users to be cautious when connecting to public Wi-Fi networks and verify the legitimacy of the network before joining.
whyWrong: Impersonation is pretending to be a person, not setting up a fake network.
An insider threat comes from someone inside the organization.
Whaling is phishing aimed at executives.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 65

stem: A user receives a call from someone who claims to be from the user’s bank and requests information to ensure the user’s account is safe. Which of the following social engineering attacks is the user experiencing?
explanation: The user in this scenario is experiencing a social engineering attack known as vishing. Vishing is a type of attack where the attacker attempts to deceive individuals by phone calls, pretending to be a trusted entity such as a bank representative. They aim to extract sensitive information, such as account details or personal data, from unsuspecting victims. It is important for users to be cautious and never provide personal information over the phone unless they can verify the legitimacy of the caller.
whyWrong: Phishing uses email or fake websites.
Smishing uses text messages.
Whaling targets executives.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 79

stem: As part of your training program, you're trying to educate users on the importance of security. You explain to them that not every attack depends on implementing advanced technological methods. Some attacks, you explain, take advantage of human shortcomings to gain access that should otherwise be denied. Which term do you use to describe attacks of this type?
explanation: Social engineering uses the inherent trust in the human species, as opposed to technology, to gain access to your environment. IDSs are network-based systems that detect intrusions. Perimeter security describes physical security. Biometrics describes an authentication method based on human physical traits.
whyWrong: An intrusion detection system is a technical control that watches the network for attacks, not an attack type.
Perimeter security is a physical security layer, not an attack that exploits human trust.
Biometrics is an authentication method based on physical traits, not an attack on people.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which type of attack denies authorized users access to network resources?
explanation: Although the end result of any of these attacks may be denying authorized users access to network resources, a denial-of-service (DoS) attack is specifically intended to prevent access to network resources by overwhelming or flooding a service or network. Worms reproduce and move throughout the network to infect other systems. Trojans are programs that enter a system or network under the guise of another program. Social engineering is a process in which an attacker attempts to acquire information about your network and system by social means, such as talking to people in the organization.
whyWrong: A worm copies itself across the network to infect other systems; denying access is not its defining goal.
A Trojan hides inside a program that looks legitimate; it is not defined by flooding a service.
Social engineering tricks people into giving information; it does not flood a network service.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 5

stem: As the security administrator for your organization, you must be aware of all types of attacks that can occur and plan for them. Which type of attack uses more than one computer to attack the victim?
explanation: A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack uses multiple computer systems to attack a server or host in the network. A denial-of-service (DoS) is a one-on-one attack to disrupt service. Worms reproduce and move throughout the network to infect other systems and therefore do not attack one victim. Rootkits are software programs that have the ability to hide themselves from the operating system.
whyWrong: A denial-of-service attack comes from one system, not from many computers at once.
A worm spreads itself to many systems rather than using many systems against one victim.
A rootkit hides itself from the operating system; it is not an attack from many computers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 6

stem: You've discovered that credentials to a specific application have been stolen. The application is accessed from only one computer on the network. Which type of attack is this MOST LIKELY to be?
explanation: An on-path attack intercepts data and then sends the information to the server as if nothing were wrong, while collecting the information. Zero-day attacks are attacks in which a developer has not properly patched a hole yet and is unaware of the hole. A denial-of-service (DoS) attack is used to disrupt legitimate requests from being answered. A Smurf attack is a type of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS).
whyWrong: A zero-day attack exploits an unpatched flaw that the vendor does not know about yet, not intercepted credentials.
A denial-of-service attack blocks access to a service; it does not steal credentials.
A Smurf attack is a flood of ICMP traffic that denies service; it does not capture credentials.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 8

stem: A junior administrator comes to you in a panic. After looking at the log files, he has become convinced that an attacker is attempting to use a legitimate IP address to disrupt access elsewhere on the network. Which type of attack is this?
explanation: A spoofing attack is an attempt by someone or something to masquerade as someone else (IP address) and is often used to disrupt access. Social engineering is a process in which an attacker attempts to acquire information about your network and system by social means, such as talking to people in the organization. Worms reproduce and move throughout the network to infect other systems. Password attacks are used in an attempt to guess passwords.
whyWrong: Social engineering tricks people, but this attack uses a forged IP address on the network.
A worm spreads copies of itself; it does not pose as a legitimate IP address.
A password attack tries to guess passwords; it does not forge an IP address.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 9

stem: A reflective attack attempts to use a broadcast ping on a network. The return address of the ping may be that of a valid system in your network. Which protocol does the reflective attack use to conduct the attack?
explanation: The reflective attack is using a broadcast ping (ICMP) on a network. The return address of the ping may be that of a valid system in your network. The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is not typically used with a reflective attack. The Internet Protocol (IP) is a suite of protocols and solely used with a reflective attack. The User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is not described in this reflective attack.
whyWrong: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol and is not what a broadcast ping uses.
IP carries the packets, but the ping that the attack sends is an ICMP message.
UDP is a connectionless transport protocol; a ping uses ICMP, not UDP.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 11

stem: Which type of attack involves passing a database query with a web request?
explanation: A SQL injection attack is a method of passing a SQL query with a web request by using an escape code sequence. An insider threat is a threat from within your organization, such as a disgruntled employee. An evil twin attack involves a rogue access point with the same SSID as your organization. Tailgating is the act of walking behind someone who has swiped to get into an area so the attacker can gain entry.
whyWrong: An insider threat comes from a person inside the organization, not from a query in a web request.
An evil twin is a rogue access point with a trusted SSID, not a database attack.
Tailgating is following someone through a secured door, not a web attack.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 5: Security Concepts, Review Questions question 12

stem: Your help desk has informed you that they received an urgent call from the vice president last night requesting his login ID and password. When you talk with the VP today, he says he never made that call. What type of attack is this?
explanation: Spear phishing is a type of social engineering, where someone is trying to con your organization into revealing account and password information by pretending to be a high-level person. A spoofing attack is an attempt by someone or something to masquerade as someone else, with the intent of disrupting access.
