explanation: The least privilege policy is designed to minimize the potential damage or unauthorized access that can occur when a user’s account is compromised or misused. By limiting user privileges, the policy reduces the attack surface and limits the ability of an attacker to move laterally within a system or network.
whyWrong: Power Users is a group kept for backward compatibility and does not limit users to their tasks.
Disabling guest accounts is good practice but does not limit the rights of normal users.
Renaming the administrator account hides it from attackers but does not prevent over-privileged users.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.6 question 2

stem: Which of the following is NOT a recommended practice for creating a strong password?
options: Using a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters
Including personal information such as your name or birthdate
Making it at least eight characters long
explanation: Including personal information such as your name or date of birth is not a best practice to create a strong password as personal information can be easily guessed. Attackers often try such details first when guessing passwords.
whyWrong: Mixing uppercase and lowercase letters adds complexity, so it is a recommended practice.
Special characters and numbers protect against guessing and dictionary attacks, so they are recommended.
A longer password increases the number of combinations to guess, so length is recommended.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.6 question 3

stem: A technician has disabled support for Wake-on-LAN (WoL) network support. This is a requirement for all company laptop computers. The technician is concerned that users will simply turn this feature back on. What is the most effective way to block this action?
options: Enable Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) passwords
Ensure user passwords have complexity requirements set
Ensure user passwords have expiration requirements set
Ensure user passwords have length requirements
explanation: UEFI replaces the older Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) and holds settings such as boot options and hardware configurations. To prevent a user from tampering with any settings, a password should be set.
whyWrong: Password complexity strengthens user passwords but does not stop changes to firmware settings.
Password expiration forces regular changes but does not protect the firmware configuration.
Password length rules strengthen user passwords but do not lock the UEFI settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.6 question 4

stem: A CISO is preparing guidance for company employees on the use of password managers. What is the purpose of a password manager?
explanation: A password manager is a software application or service that helps you securely store and manage your passwords. It provides a convenient way to generate, store, and retrieve complex passwords for different online accounts. A password manager will also protect passwords using encryption.
whyWrong: Generating passwords is only one of the purposes, so this choice alone is incomplete.
Storing and organizing passwords is only one of the purposes, so this choice alone is incomplete.
Encrypting passwords is only one of the purposes, so this choice alone is incomplete.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.6 question 5

stem: An administrator must ensure that contract personnel employed in the payroll team will only be able to log in to the network when other members of staff are present. What would be the most effective way to ensure this is enforced?
options: Restrict user permissions outside of core business hours
Restrict login times for contractors to core business hours
Disable guest accounts on all contractors’ workstations
Ensure contractors’ accounts are locked out after three failed attempts
explanation: Restricting login times for contractors to core business hours will restrict the ability of the contractors to log on to systems unless other members of the payroll staff are present. The account simply cannot sign in outside the allowed hours.
whyWrong: Restricting permissions outside business hours still lets the contractors log in at any time.
The contractors have their own accounts, so disabling guest accounts has no effect here.
Lockout after failed attempts is good practice but does not control when contractors can log in.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.6 question 6

stem: An administrator is concerned that an attacker can gain access to a user’s account by using a dictionary attack at the login prompt. What security setting would be the most effective?
options: Enforce a minimum password length of 10 characters
Restrict login times for contractors to core business hours
Disable guest accounts on all workstations
Ensure accounts are locked out after three failed attempts
explanation: Account lockout will prevent attacks against the interactive login process. Any automated attacks using wordlists or brute force will be highly unlikely to succeed.
whyWrong: A minimum length does not stop a user from choosing a password that is in a word list.
Login hours do not help if the attacker tries the dictionary attack during permitted hours.
Disabling guest accounts has no effect on attacks against other user accounts.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.6 question 8

stem: A senior manager raises a support ticket after encountering a problem during an important presentation. The manager inserted a memory card, to access the presentation material, and a movie file began to play. What can a support technician do to resolve the ticket?
options: Configure autoplay settings for memory cards
Configure autoplay settings for removable drives
Ensure Windows Movie Player is blocked from playing
explanation: By configuring autoplay settings for memory cards, the action can be set to do nothing. The card will be recognized but no automated actions will be taken.
whyWrong: Blocking external media would also make the presentation material unavailable.
The removable drives setting is the wrong AutoPlay option because the media is a memory card.
Blocking the movie player may partly help but does not stop AutoPlay from acting on the card.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.6 question 9

stem: Which of the following is the best practice for maintaining password security?
options: Sharing passwords with trusted family members or friends
Using the same password across multiple accounts
Writing down passwords on a piece of paper and keeping it in a visible place
explanation: By changing your password on a regular basis, you will reduce the risk of someone using stolen credentials to access your accounts, counteracting password-guessing or cracking attacks, and limit the impact of stolen passwords. Password expiration is one of the password considerations in the objectives.
whyWrong: Sharing passwords with family or friends exposes the account to other people.
Reusing one password means a single breach exposes every account that uses it.
A visible written password can be read by anyone who passes the desk.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.6 question 10
note: 220-1102 2.6; mapped to 220-1202 2.7 (password considerations). Current NIST guidance prefers changing a password when it may be compromised over forced frequent changes, but this is still the only good option here.

stem: A CISO must ensure the company is compliant with recommended best security practices. The CISO has noticed that on occasion, users’ laptops are displaying personally identifiable information (PII) and intellectual property (IP) when users are not at their desks. What would be the most effective control to secure the workstations?
options: Use a timeout to automatically enable screen locks
Have all users read and sign an acceptable use policy (AUP)
Have all users lock their laptops in a secure location whenever they leave their desks
Use cable locks to secure the laptops to desks
explanation: A timeout that enables screen locks ensures the screens are locked after a period of inactivity (this can be as short as 1 minute). This protects PII and intellectual property when users leave their desks.
whyWrong: An acceptable use policy reminds users of their duties but does not lock an unattended screen.
Locking laptops away each time users leave their desks is impractical.
Cable locks stop theft of the laptop but leave the screen and its data visible.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.6 question 11

stem: A service desk operator takes a call from a user who suspects that their password has been compromised. What would be the operator’s BEST recommended action for the user?
options: Continue using the same password but monitor account activity closely
Immediately change the password for the affected account
Delete the account and create a new one
Do nothing and hope for the best
explanation: The password should be changed in the first instance, to protect the account. After changing the password, additional monitoring of account activity would also be good advice.
whyWrong: Keeping a compromised password lets an attacker keep using the account while it is monitored.
Deleting the account is impractical, as it may hold encryption keys or certificates that are then lost.
Doing nothing leaves the compromised account open to the attacker.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.6 question 12

stem: What is a major security concern when considering the deployment of IoT devices, when used in building automation systems?
explanation: IoT devices will connect to wireless networks and will be vulnerable if the default account password is not changed. Attackers know the default credentials that manufacturers use.
whyWrong: Zigbee is a wireless protocol for personal area networks in home automation, not the main concern.
Resilient mesh networks help provide a strong wireless signal and are not a security concern.
Location services report where a device is, which is not the major concern for building automation.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.7 question 6

stem: Lee, a lab technician at a school, finds that students change the boot order of the lab PCs to start them from their own USB drives. The PCs must still start Windows without a password. Which measure is BEST?
explanation: A supervisor password protects the BIOS/UEFI setup utility, so firmware settings such as the boot order cannot be changed. The PCs still start normally because no password is needed at boot.
whyWrong: A system password asks for a password at every startup, which the school does not want.
BitLocker protects the stored data but does not stop a change to the firmware boot order.
Disabling the Guest account protects Windows sign-in, not the firmware settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

stem: A contractor will work at an accounting office for three months. The office manager wants the contractor's Windows account to stop working on the last day even if IT forgets about it. Which action is BEST?
options: Set logon hours on the account
explanation: An account expiration date disables the account automatically on the chosen day. It suits temporary employees and contractors whose end date is known.
whyWrong: The lockout threshold blocks an account after failed sign-ins, not on a set date.
Logon hours limit the hours of the day for sign-ins but do not end the account.
Renaming the Administrator account protects the built-in admin, not a contractor's account.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

stem: Users at a design office often plug in USB drives from trade shows. The security lead wants nothing on the drives to run before the drives are scanned. Which setting is BEST?
explanation: With AutoPlay off, removable media cannot start an AutoRun program on its own, so malware on it does not run before the scan. It can be turned off in Settings or with the Turn off AutoPlay Group Policy setting.
whyWrong: Disabling unused services shrinks the attack surface but does not stop media from starting programs.
Password history stops reused passwords and has nothing to do with removable media.
A screen saver lock protects an unattended PC, not a PC that has a USB drive inserted.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

stem: You’ve lost your iPhone. What would you use to try to find it?
explanation: Apple’s iPhone uses the Find My iPhone feature of iCloud. Find My can also play a sound, lock the device, or erase it remotely.
whyWrong: iTunes manages media and backups; it does not locate a lost phone.
iFind is not an Apple service.
Location Services lets apps use the location, but you need iCloud's Find My to see where the phone is.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 25: Maintaining and Securing Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 4

stem: A great way to protect data on a removable media card is to ___________.
explanation: A great way to protect data on a removable media card is to encrypt it. Encrypted data stays unreadable even when the card is lost or stolen.
whyWrong: A physical lock switch on a card stops writes but does not protect data if the card is taken.
Removing the card helps, but the data is still readable if the card is lost.
Formatting erases the data instead of protecting it.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 25: Maintaining and Securing Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 7

stem: Users bringing personally owned mobile devices into an enterprise environment is called ___________.
explanation: Users bringing personally owned mobile device into an enterprise environment is known as bring your own device (BYOD). A BYOD policy sets the rules that personal devices must meet before they connect to company resources.
whyWrong: Importing is not the term for bringing personal devices into the workplace.
CMYK is a color model for printing, not a device policy.
Providing is not the term for bringing personal devices into the workplace.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 25: Maintaining and Securing Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 9

stem: What do app scanners do?
options: Scan QR codes and barcodes for hidden codes
Analyze the traffic into and out of an application for suspicious behavior
Analyze the permissions used by installed applications to highlight security risks
Analyze Wi-Fi signals to identify evil-twin WAPs
explanation: App scanners analyze the permissions used by installed applications to highlight security risks. Apps that ask for more permissions than they need can be a sign of spyware.
whyWrong: Scanning QR codes and barcodes is the job of a reader app, not an app scanner.
Watching an app's traffic is the work of a network monitor or firewall.
Finding evil-twin access points is the job of a wireless analyzer.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 25: Maintaining and Securing Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 10

stem: Which of the following is the BEST way to maintain data security for a mobile device that has been lost or stolen?
explanation: The best answer to maintain data security is to initiate a remote wipe on a device that has been lost or stolen. That will delete the data and make it very difficult to reconstruct.
whyWrong: A passcode lock only slows down someone who has the device.
GPS can help find the device, but it does not protect the data on it.
Login attempt restrictions only slow down someone who has the device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 78

stem: A user has installed unapproved utilities and applications on a mobile phone. The company has recently deployed MDM tools and would like to prevent users from sideloading unapproved applications. What two MDM policies will prevent future users from sideloading unapproved applications?
explanation: App whitelisting is a mobile device management (MDM) policy that allows administrators to specify which applications are allowed to be installed on mobile devices. By creating a whitelist of approved applications, you can prevent users from sideloading unapproved applications because only the apps on the whitelist can be installed. You can also restrict users from sideloading apps by enforcing policies that only allow app installations from official app stores (such as Google Play or the Apple App Store).
whyWrong: USB debugging is a developer option and does not stop sideloading by itself.
Device encryption protects data but does not stop sideloading.
Remote wipe protects data on a lost device but does not stop sideloading.
Geofencing triggers actions by location and does not stop sideloading.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 24

stem: What is the purpose of the remote wipe feature on a stolen mobile phone?
options: To physically retrieve the stolen device
To track the location of the stolen device
To delete all data on the stolen device remotely
To disable the stolen device’s network connectivity
explanation: The remote wipe feature allows the owner of a stolen mobile phone to remotely erase all data stored on the device. This helps protect sensitive information from falling into the wrong hands. Tracking the location of the device is typically handled by other features, like GPS or cellular location services.
whyWrong: A remote wipe runs over the network and cannot bring the physical device back to its owner.
Tracking the device is the job of a locator application, not of a remote wipe.
A remote wipe erases the data; cutting network access is not its purpose.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 33

stem: Which policy would you create to define the minimum specification if an employee wanted to use their own device for email?
explanation: A bring your own device (BYOD) policy defines the minimum specifications for an employee's device used for work-related access. The mobile device management (MDM) software would usually police these specifications, but it would not define them. The acceptable use policy (AUP) is a code of conduct when dealing with organization resources. The nondisclosure agreement (NDA) is an agreement used when dealing with intellectual property.
whyWrong: MDM software enforces device settings, but the policy that defines the minimum specification is the BYOD policy.
An acceptable use policy sets the code of conduct for organization resources, not device specifications.
A nondisclosure agreement protects confidential information, not the specifications of a personal device.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 1

stem: Which term refers to copying data between a mobile device and a computer system in order to mirror such things as contacts, programs, pictures, and music?
explanation: Synchronizing a mobile device with a computer system allows you to mirror personal data between the devices, regardless of which one contains the most current data. Calibration refers to matching the device's and the user's perceptions of where the user is touching the screen. Remote wipes allow you to remove personal data from a lost or stolen device. Pairing is what must be done in Bluetooth for two Bluetooth devices to connect and communicate.
whyWrong: Calibration aligns the touchscreen with where the user touches; it does not copy data.
A remote wipe erases data from a lost or stolen device; it does not mirror data.
Pairing connects two Bluetooth devices; it does not copy contacts and files between them.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 2
note: Mobile device synchronization is a 220-1201 topic; mapped to 220-1202 2.8.6 (remote backup applications).

stem: What kind of mobile app is being used when the owner’s phone displays a message on the screen and emits an extremely loud tone?
explanation: Locator apps can find the phone and then display a message that can be read even while the phone is locked. Locator apps also often give the user the option to make the phone blare a noise to aid in finding the device. Failed login restrictions will wipe a device if a specific number of wrong passwords are entered. Remotely wiping a mobile device is a feature of locator apps, but it is not itself an app that displays messages and produces noises.
whyWrong: A failed login restriction locks or wipes a device after wrong passwords; it does not sound an alarm.
An antivirus app protects against malware but cannot show a message or play a tone to find the phone.
A remote wipe erases the device and is one feature of a locator app, not the app that plays a tone.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 4

stem: By default, when setting up an Android device, why do you need a Google account?
options: The account is used for cloud synchronizations.
The account is used for desktop backups.
explanation: By default, a Google account is required on Android devices; it is used to synchronize data and app purchases to the cloud. The device does not require email to be set up, but the account can be used for the setup. The account is not used for desktop backups. The device does not require registration.
whyWrong: Android does not require email to be set up, although the Google account can be used for it.
The Google account synchronizes to the cloud, not to backups of a desktop computer.
Android devices do not require a separate registration during setup.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 13

stem: You need to secure your mobile device’s lock screen with the highest level of protection. Which of the following should you use? (Choose the BEST answer.)
explanation: Fingerprint locks are the most secure of all the lock methods, since fingerprints are hard to duplicate. Face locks have a high number of false positives, which can be used to gain access to the phone. Passcode locks can be cracked or shoulder surfed. Swipe locks are not really locks; they just allow the screen to be opened with a swipe.
whyWrong: Face locks have a high rate of false positives that can let someone else into the phone.
A passcode can be cracked or seen by someone looking over the user's shoulder.
A swipe lock is not a real lock because anyone can open the screen with a swipe.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 14

stem: You need to enforce profile security requirements on mobile devices. Which should you use to achieve this goal?
explanation: Mobile device management (MDM) software enables you to enforce profile security requirements on mobile devices. The acceptable use policy (AUP) is a code of ethics your users should follow when dealing with organizational resources. A nondisclosure agreement (NDA) is an agreement between an employee and the organization to protect intellectual property. A bring your own device (BYOD) policy explains how devices should be secured but provides no enforcement.
whyWrong: An acceptable use policy sets rules of conduct but cannot enforce settings on devices.
A nondisclosure agreement protects intellectual property; it does not enforce device profiles.
A BYOD policy explains how devices should be secured but has no way to enforce it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 20

stem: You want to prevent a user from accessing your phone while you step away from your desk. What should you do?
options: Set up a remote wipe program.
explanation: You should configure a screen lock (either a pattern drawn on the screen, a PIN, a password, biometric recognition, or something else). Remote backup, remote wipe, and locator applications will not prevent someone from accessing the phone. A screen lock is a basic hardening technique that should be set to start after a short idle period.
whyWrong: Remote backup saves the phone's data elsewhere but does not stop someone from using the phone.
A remote wipe erases a lost device's data later; it does not stop access while you step away.
A locator application finds a lost device; it does not stop someone from opening the phone.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which of the following can be described as removing limitations in iOS?
explanation: Jailbreaking is the process of removing the limitations of an iOS-based device so that the user gets superuser abilities. Rooting is a similar technique used on Android mobile devices. Geotracking is the practice of tracking a device over time. Antivirus software is used to combat malware.
whyWrong: Rooting is the similar technique used on Android devices, not on iOS.
Geotracking is tracking a device's location over time, not removing operating system limits.
Antivirus software combats malware; it does not remove iOS limitations.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security, Cram Quiz question 2
note: Jailbreaking is a 220-1202 3.3 security concern; the book places it in 2.8 hardening.

stem: Your organization is concerned about a potential scenario involving a mobile device containing confidential data being stolen. Which of the following should be recommended FIRST? (Select the best answer.)
explanation: The remote wipe program is the most important option listed. This will prevent a thief from accessing the data on the device. Afterward, you might recommend a backup program (in case the data needs to be wiped), as well as passcode locks and a locator application.
whyWrong: A remote backup application saves the data but does not stop a thief from reading it.
A passcode lock helps, but a thief may still get past it, while a remote wipe removes the data.
A locator application may find the device, but it does not protect the confidential data on it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: You are concerned about the possibility of jailbreaks on your organization’s iPhones and viruses on the Android-based devices. Which of the following should you implement? (Select the two BEST answers.)
explanation: You should implement antivirus software on the local mobile devices and consider MDM for deploying antivirus updates to multiple mobile devices remotely. This can protect against viruses and other malware as well as jailbreaks on Apple devices. As of the writing of this book, firewalls for mobile devices are not common, but that could change in the future. Device resets are used to restart mobile devices or to reset them to factory condition, depending on the type of reset and the manufacturer of a device. We’ll discuss those more in Chapter 54, “Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications.”
whyWrong: Firewalls for mobile devices are not common and do not address jailbreaks or viruses.
A device reset restarts a device or restores factory condition; it does not prevent jailbreaks or viruses.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Android-based smartphones in your organization are part of the BYOD infrastructure. They need to be able to connect to the LAN remotely using a VPN. Which of the following should you incorporate into the MDM profile for the smartphones to connect to the VPN securely? (Select the BEST answer.)
explanation: Use an encryption certificate to secure the VPN connection process from the mobile devices to the LAN. Antivirus software is important for mobile devices, but it won’t impact secure VPN connectivity. Remote wipe is an important theft/loss solution. Authenticator apps are used to verify a user to a system and are often used in place of the second step of two-factor authentication, but they are not as secure as using a certificate. Microsoft Intune can be used to administer mobile devices, but it is not inherently secure; the profiles therein need to be configured in a secure way.
whyWrong: Antivirus software protects the device from malware but does not secure the VPN connection.
A remote wipe protects data on a lost or stolen device; it does not secure VPN connections.
An authenticator app verifies the user but is not as secure as a certificate for the VPN connection.
Microsoft Intune is an MDM tool to manage devices; it is not secure until its profiles are configured.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which of the following is a primary function of a mobile device management (MDM) suite?
options: Primarily managing corporate-owned software and applications on mobile devices
Securing, monitoring, managing, and supporting different types of mobile devices across an enterprise from a central location
Focusing on separating personal data and applications from work data on employee-owned devices
Primarily addressing the logistical problems associated with employees using personal devices for work purposes
explanation: Decent-quality MDM software will secure, monitor, manage, and support different types of mobile devices across the enterprise. An MDM server can take care of pushing updates and configuring hundreds of mobile devices from a central location. Contrast this with mobile application management (MAM), which concerns corporate-owned software and apps. While MDM can be used to create separate partitions or containers, it as a capability within the broader functions of MDM, not its primary focus. While MDM can help manage BYOD devices, the logistical problems themselves are broader and include user agreements and data loss prevention strategies, which aren't solely the domain of MDM.
whyWrong: Managing corporate-owned apps on mobile devices is the focus of mobile application management.
Separating personal and work data is one capability of MDM, not its primary function.
BYOD logistics include user agreements and data loss prevention, which go beyond the main job of MDM.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: What is a significant concern for organizations when implementing a bring-your-own-device (BYOD) policy?
options: The potential difficulty in managing updates for a variety of device operating systems
The loss of employee privacy due to organizational monitoring of personal devices
The increased risk of data leakage and other security breaches related to mobile devices
The complexity of initially configuring personal devices for work use
explanation: From a company perspective, the greatest concern is the leakage of data and any other security breaches related to mobile devices. While managing updates can be a challenge in a BYOD environment, MDM is a solution for pushing updates, suggesting it's a manageable issue. The "greatest concern" from a company perspective is explicitly stated as data leakage. The loss of employee privacy as "the greatest concern" is from a user perspective, not necessarily the primary concern for the organization. While initial configuration can be complex, data leakage is a more prominent concern for the organization.
whyWrong: Updates for many operating systems are a challenge, but MDM can push updates to manage this.
Loss of privacy is a concern from the user's side, not the main concern for the organization.
Initial setup can be complex, but data leakage is the more important concern for the organization.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: A user wants to check manually for an operating system update on an iPhone. Where should the user go?
options: Settings, then General, then Software Update
Settings, then Privacy & Security, then Location Services
Settings, then General, then Transfer or Reset iPhone
explanation: On iOS and iPadOS devices, operating system updates are under Settings, General, Software Update. Devices also notify the user about updates, but users should check regularly in case a notice does not appear. Installing the updates soon after release fixes known security flaws.
whyWrong: The Battery screen shows battery usage and health and does not check for OS updates.
Location Services controls which apps can use the device's location, not operating system updates.
Transfer or Reset iPhone moves data or resets the device; it does not install updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

stem: By default, how do Android and iOS devices install automatic app updates?
options: Over Wi-Fi, but not over cellular data
Over cellular data only, to save Wi-Fi bandwidth
Only when the user opens each app
Only after the operating system is updated
explanation: Both the Google Play Store and the Apple App Store can update apps automatically in the background. By default, they do this over Wi-Fi and not over cellular data. Users can change this in the app store settings to allow updates over cellular data as well.
whyWrong: The default is the opposite, because app stores avoid using metered cellular data for updates.
Automatic updates install in the background without the user opening each app.
App updates install on their own schedule and do not wait for an operating system update.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

stem: An IT manager wants to push OS and app updates to all company phones from one console and see which phones are behind on patches. Which solution BEST meets this need?
explanation: MDM software manages many mobile devices from one central console. Patch management is one of its tasks, along with app and content management. It can deploy updates to many devices at once and report which ones are out of date.
whyWrong: A locator application finds a lost device on a map; it does not deploy or report on updates.
A remote backup application copies device data to the cloud but does not manage patches.
Content filtering blocks unwanted websites and content; it does not push OS or app updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 47: Social Engineering, Threats, and Vulnerabilities

stem: An iPhone has a passcode, but its Erase Data setting is turned off. Someone keeps entering wrong passcodes over many lockouts. What finally happens?
options: The phone cannot be unlocked until it is connected to the computer it last synced with
The phone deletes all data at once after the third wrong passcode
The phone unlocks after a 24-hour timeout with no further limits
The phone switches to an unlock method that uses only a fingerprint
explanation: Even with Erase Data off, iOS adds lockout periods that get longer after each set of wrong passcodes. The final penalty is that the device cannot be unlocked until it is connected to the computer it last synced with. With Erase Data on, the device would instead wipe its data after 10 wrong passcodes.
whyWrong: Erasing the data is the Erase Data setting, which is off here, and it acts after 10 attempts, not three.
The lockout periods get longer, and they do not end with an unlimited unlock after one day.
Failed passcodes do not switch the phone to fingerprint-only unlock; biometrics still need the passcode.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

stem: A call center manager is proposing to support an initiative where workers will be able to work from home. The security team is discussing methods that will allow the use of personal equipment and the control and management of employees’ personal devices. Which of the following controls allows the team to manage this infrastructure and ensure users are given guidance to support this initiative? (Choose two.)
explanation: A BYOD policy allows for standards and guidelines to be addressed for the use of personal equipment to access business systems. Mobile device management (MDM) allows the team to manage and configure a wide range of mobile devices.
whyWrong: A fingerprint scanner secures authentication but gives no guidance or management for personal devices.
MFA strengthens the login process but does not manage personal devices or set rules for their use.
Equipment locks physically secure hardware and do not manage personal devices used from home.
Time-based login policies limit when accounts sign in; they do not manage or guide personal device use.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.1 question 3
note: 220-1102 2.1 (MDM, BYOD); mapped to 220-1202 2.8 (mobile device policies and procedures).

stem: An administrator is following best practices by ensuring that company-issued mobile devices have preventative controls enabled to ensure the privacy of stored data, in the event of the loss or theft of the devices. What two settings will be most effective?
options: Screen lock with a password with a minimum of 10 characters
explanation: A screen lock will prevent unauthorized access to the mobile device and FDE ensures the data is protected. After a predetermined number of unsuccessful password attempts, the data is rendered unrecoverable.
whyWrong: Restrictive firewall settings protect the device on a network but not the stored data after theft.
An always-on VPN protects network traffic, not data stored on a lost device.
A BYOD acceptable use policy sets rules but does little to protect a lost or stolen device.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.7 question 1

stem: Which of the following statements accurately describes a security concern specific to bring your own device (BYOD)?
options: BYOD devices have limited compatibility with corporate applications
COBO devices may compromise employee privacy and personal data
BYOD increases the risk of unauthorized data access through lost or stolen devices
COBO devices are more susceptible to phishing attacks and social engineering
explanation: In a BYOD scenario, if an employee’s personal device is lost or stolen, there is an increased risk of unauthorized individuals gaining access to sensitive corporate data stored on the device. Since BYOD devices are not under full control of the organization, it can be more challenging to implement robust security measures such as remote wiping or encryption. This risk highlights the importance of strong security policies and protocols for BYOD, such as password protection, device tracking, and data encryption.
whyWrong: Compatibility issues with corporate apps can affect both BYOD and company-owned devices.
Privacy and personal data problems can occur with both BYOD and company-owned devices if poorly managed.
Phishing and social engineering can affect any device, whoever owns it.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.7 question 2

stem: An international bank issues smartphones to some employees and allows the use of personal devices for other staff members. It is important that audio and video recordings can be restricted when devices are taken into restricted areas. What would allow mobile devices to be managed in this way? (Choose two.)
explanation: By deploying mobile device management (MDM), configuration settings can be enforced. Geofencing allows a virtual fence or boundary to be set when the device is geolocated within the fence, and then the settings can be enforced.
whyWrong: BYOD only describes using personal devices for work and does not enforce any settings.
Screen locks protect a lost or stolen device but do not restrict recording in certain areas.
Device encryption protects data on a lost device but does not disable audio or video recording.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.7 question 4

stem: An organization needs to store data on a mobile device that will include PII and proprietary information. The organization has already implemented FDE and screen locks. In order to add another layer of security, there is a requirement for users to authenticate using biometrics. Which of the following could be used to satisfy the organizational requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation: Facial recognition and fingerprint would satisfy the requirements for biometrics (something you are). PIN codes, patterns, and swipes are something you know or no factor at all.
whyWrong: A PIN code is something you know, not a biometric.
A pattern is something you know, not a biometric.
A swipe is not a biometric and gives almost no security.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.7 question 5

stem: Rosa, a sales manager, reports that her company phone was stolen from her car. It holds client contracts, it is still online, and she does not expect to get it back. Which action is BEST?
options: Send a remote wipe to the phone
Track the phone with a locator app
Install an OS update on the phone
Turn on content filtering for the phone
explanation: A remote wipe erases the phone's contents from another computer or an MDM server while the phone can still reach the internet. It keeps the client data from being read after the theft.
whyWrong: A locator app helps get a device back, but Rosa does not expect to recover it and the data is at risk.
An OS update fixes flaws but does not protect data on a phone that a thief already has.
Content filtering blocks websites and does nothing for the data on a stolen phone.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

stem: A marketing firm lets employees read company email on their own phones. Employees worry about their privacy, and the firm must be able to remove its data when someone leaves. Which approach is BEST?
options: Use MDM to keep work apps and data in a separate container
Turn on the erase data option after 10 failed passcodes
Issue every employee a corporate-owned phone
Install a locator app on each phone
explanation: In a BYOD setting, MDM can separate the work apps and data from the personal ones with containerization. The firm can remove its own data without touching the employee's personal files.
whyWrong: Erasing after failed passcodes would wipe personal data too and does not separate work data.
Corporate-owned phones remove the BYOD arrangement the firm wants to keep.
A locator app finds a lost phone but does not separate or remove company data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

stem: An attorney's iPhone holds sensitive case files and is often used in courtrooms and cafes. A recent backup is always kept in iCloud. Which setting BEST protects the data if someone keeps guessing the passcode?
options: Erase the data after 10 failed passcode attempts
explanation: This failed log-in restriction wipes the iPhone after 10 wrong passcodes in a row. It suits a user with sensitive data who takes the phone to public places and always has a recent backup.
whyWrong: A swipe lock has no real security and makes guessing even easier.
App updates fix flaws in apps but do nothing against passcode guessing.
The backup is already in place; it saves the data but does not protect it from the person guessing.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

stem: Which of the following is not a way to physically destroy data on a hard drive?
explanation: Low-level formatting does not physically destroy the hard drive, allowing it to be reused. Drilling, shredding, and degaussing leave the drive unusable, while a formatted drive can still be reused.
whyWrong: Drilling holes through the platters physically destroys a hard drive.
Shredding tears the drive into small pieces and physically destroys it.
Degaussing uses a strong magnetic field that destroys the data on a magnetic drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 11: Installing and Upgrading Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 1

stem: Which of the following are ways to remove data from a storage drive through destruction? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: A drive shredder or drill can be used to physically tear the drive into multiple pieces or to make holes in the platters of the hard drive, thus making it inoperable. It can then be disposed of according to municipal guidelines. This is one of several ways to physically destroy a drive and is performed only when the drive has met the end of its life cycle, is not going to be recycled within the organization, and is to be disposed of. However, shredding (or pulverizing) is the best way to destroy a drive; vendors offer services to perform this work and provide a certificate of destruction when complete.
whyWrong: Disabling ports blocks network access; it does not remove data from a drive.
Low-level formatting removes data but does not physically destroy the drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 28

stem: An asset disposal company needs to ensure potential customers that sensitive data will be rendered uncoverable when it is sent for destruction. When it comes to the physical destruction of SSDs containing sensitive information, which method is considered the most effective?
explanation: The best method for physically destroying SSDs that contain sensitive information is shredding. Shredding involves using specialized equipment to physically break the SSD into tiny pieces, rendering the data completely irretrievable. This method ensures the highest level of data destruction and mitigates the risk of unauthorized access or data recovery attempts. It is a recommended practice for organizations that handle sensitive information and need to comply with data privacy regulations.
whyWrong: Overwriting is not reliable on SSDs because of wear leveling.
Formatting does not reliably destroy the data.
Deleting leaves data that can be recovered.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 72

stem: A drive needs to be disposed of in such a way that no one can access the data. Which method should be used?
explanation: You should destroy the drive. You could do this with the use of a tool (such as a drive shredder), by incinerating it, or by degaussing it, although the first option is usually preferred. The format E: command will only format the drive to a new file system; that is not secure enough if the data has to be removed altogether. Clearing is the removal of data from a drive that is to be repurposed and used again within the organization. The diskpart utility can be used to clear the drive, but it is not appropriate for drive disposal.
whyWrong: format E: only writes a new file system, which is not secure enough when the data must be gone.
Clearing removes data from a drive that is reused inside the organization, not one being disposed of.
diskpart can clear a drive, but clearing is not appropriate when a drive is disposed of.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 50: Data Destruction and Disposal, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: A drive is to be repurposed within your company. You have been tasked with zeroing out the drive three times from within Windows. Which of the following methods will accomplish this?
explanation: The only option listed that will zero out the drive three times (from Windows) is format C: /fs:fat32 /p:3. This procedure formats the drive as FAT32 and runs the process three times (p:3). Degaussing a hard disk drive will render the data unreadable and, in most cases, will make the drive unusable. By default, the diskpart and dd processes listed will only zero out the drive once. Also, dd is run from Linux, not from Windows, so that is another reason that answer is incorrect.
whyWrong: Degaussing makes the data unreadable and usually the drive unusable, so the drive cannot be repurposed.
diskpart clean all zeroes the drive only once by default, not three times.
dd runs on Linux, not Windows, and this command zeroes the drive only once.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 50: Data Destruction and Disposal, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You have been tasked with purging a drive so that it can be recycled to a sister company. Which of the following should you perform before sending out the drive?
options: Run Secure Erase on the drive.
explanation: At a bare minimum, run the Secure Erase program (or a comparable program) to sanitize the drive; it needs to be completely wiped if it is to be reused. The rest of the answers are not examples of sanitizing or purging. Clearing the drive by formatting or zeroing out does not meet the requirements for sending the drive out to another company as standardized by NIST and the DoD. Degaussing the drive will render it useless. Pulverizing the drive (shredding it) will destroy it and will also render it unusable.
whyWrong: Clearing by formatting or zeroing does not meet the NIST and DoD standard for a drive sent to another company.
Degaussing makes the drive unusable, so it cannot be recycled to the sister company.
Pulverizing the drive destroys it, so it cannot be reused by the sister company.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 50: Data Destruction and Disposal, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: What is the primary reason that regulations like HIPAA and GDPR necessitate secure data destruction?
options: To ensure that organizations are using the most cost-effective methods for disposing of old hardware
To standardize the physical dimensions of storage devices being discarded
To prevent unauthorized individuals from accessing sensitive information stored on the devices
To encourage organizations to reuse old storage devices whenever possible
explanation: Regulations like HIPAA and GDPR mandate secure data erasure or physical destruction of drives to prevent unauthorized access. HIPAA focuses on protecting patient health data in the US. GDPR protects personal data of EU citizens. While cost-effectiveness might be a consideration for organizations, the security aspect is mandated by regulations, not the cost. While reuse might be possible after clearing, the regulations mentioned are concerned with destruction to prevent access.
whyWrong: Cost may matter to organizations, but the regulations require secure destruction, not the cheapest method.
The regulations say nothing about the physical size of discarded devices.
The regulations are about preventing access to data, not about encouraging reuse of old devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 50: Data Destruction and Disposal, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Why might an organization require a certificate of destruction when disposing of storage drives?
options: To ensure that the third-party vendor is using the latest technology for data erasure
To have proof that the drives were destroyed in compliance with data privacy laws
To document the chain of custody if the drives are transported offsite for destruction
To verify the resale value of the destroyed materials for accounting purposes
explanation: Many organizations require a certificate of destruction to show that a drive has indeed been destroyed; the certificate is often required by data privacy laws. While using appropriate technology is important, the certificate primarily serves as proof of destruction, not necessarily a guarantee of the latest technology being used. Chain of custody is important for tracking the drives during transport, but the certificate of destruction is a separate document confirming the completion of the destruction process. If you destroy your drives, there's a very low market for resale!
whyWrong: The certificate proves destruction took place; it does not show that the vendor uses the latest technology.
Chain of custody tracks drives during transport; the certificate of destruction is a separate document.
Destroyed drives have almost no resale value, and the certificate is not about accounting.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 50: Data Destruction and Disposal, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Why do many governments regulate how organizations dispose of old computers and other e-waste?
options: The equipment can release lead, mercury, and cadmium into soil and water
The equipment must be returned to the maker to renew its warranty
Regulations require all computers to be stored for ten years
Old equipment is the main source of network malware
explanation: Computer equipment contains hazardous materials such as lead, mercury, and cadmium. If it is dumped in a landfill, these materials can contaminate soil and water. E-waste laws require proper disposal or recycling, and organizations that ignore them can face fines.
whyWrong: Warranties have nothing to do with disposal rules, and disposed equipment is not returned for renewal.
No general rule requires keeping all old computers; the rules cover how they are disposed of.
Disposal rules protect the environment and data; they are not about malware on the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 5: Security Concepts

stem: A CISO is developing a company policy to ensure the correct procedures are followed when data is removed from storage. To ensure that there are no data remnants on magnetic media, what data destruction will be BEST?
explanation: Degaussing will completely remove all data from magnetic media such as mechanical hard disk drives and backup tapes. It is not possible to reverse this process.
whyWrong: Erasing leaves data remnants that recovery tools can often read.
Standard formatting only marks allocation units as free, so the data can be recovered.
Wiping overwrites data, but the book notes that some software can still recover it.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.8 question 1

stem: A technician has been tasked with rendering hard disk drives unusable as they have been used to store company intellectual property (IP). It is important the drives cannot be reused and must contain no data remnants. The technician has no access to specialist equipment. What would the BEST solution be?
explanation: Drilling would be a low-tech solution to achieve physical destruction. Drilling through disk platters will physically destroy the storage media.
whyWrong: Shredding needs specialist equipment that can be expensive, which the technician does not have.
Standard formatting leaves the drive usable and the data recoverable.
Degaussing needs a specialist degausser, which the technician does not have.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.8 question 2

stem: A government agency is working with a third-party data destruction specialist. It is important that the agency has a full audit trail for all data that is in use and for data that is to be removed. What documentation should the vendor provide to the government agency?
explanation: A certification of destruction (CoD) is a document that verifies the complete and secure destruction of sensitive or confidential materials. It is typically issued by a professional shredding or destruction service provider to ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, as well as to provide proof that the materials have been properly disposed of.
whyWrong: An NDA deters disclosure of sensitive data but does not prove that data was destroyed.
Certification of incinerating is not a certificate type; a provider that burns materials still issues a CoD.
A service-level agreement sets performance targets and does not prove destruction.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.8 question 3

stem: A manager must ensure that paper-based documentation is rendered unreadable. The documents contain data classified as secret. What two methods, when used together, would ensure classified documents are rendered unreadable?
explanation: It is common that regulatory compliance will require highly classified documents to be sanitized using shredding and incineration together. Shredding cuts the paper into small pieces and incineration burns the remains so nothing can be rebuilt.
whyWrong: Degaussing works on magnetic media such as hard drives, not on paper documents.
Erasing applies to electronic storage media and cannot be used on paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.8 question 4
note: 220-1102 2.8; mapped to 220-1202 2.9 (data destruction). The question is about paper; the 220-1202 objective lists these methods under hard drives.

stem: Which hardware firewall feature enables incoming traffic on a specific port to reach an IP address on the LAN?
explanation: To open a port on your hardware firewall and send incoming traffic to a specific PC, use port forwarding. For example, port 443 on the router can be forwarded to a web server on the LAN.
whyWrong: NAT translates private addresses to a public one but does not by itself send a port to a host.
A screened subnet is a separate network zone for public servers, not a rule for one port.
Multifactor authentication proves a user's identity; it does not route traffic.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 27: Securing Computers, Chapter Review question 4

stem: Which of these choices would provide better security for Mary’s Wi-Fi router?
explanation: Mary should set up WPA3 on her Wi-Fi router. WPA3 uses SAE for its handshake, which resists password-guessing attacks.
whyWrong: Secure DNS protects name lookups, not the wireless connection to the router.
WEP is deprecated and can be cracked quickly.
WPA2 is still secure, but WPA3 is newer and stronger.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 27: Securing Computers, Chapter Review question 6
note: 220-1102 2.2 and 2.9; mapped to 220-1202 2.10 (wireless specific: encryption settings).

stem: In a SOHO wireless network, which of the following prevents unauthorized users from accessing confidential data?
explanation: Encryption (for example, WPA3 with AES) prevents unauthorized users from accessing confidential data that is transmitted over the wireless network. One of the best ways to protect confidentiality of data in general is through encryption. Use the highest level of encryption possible on a SOHO wireless network to eliminate this threat.
whyWrong: MAC filtering stops unknown devices from joining but does not protect the data, and it can be bypassed.
Changing the SSID name only renames the network.
Reducing broadcast power shortens the range but does not protect data from someone nearby.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 69

stem: You have been tasked with setting up an AP in a small office that is in the middle of a crowded building. What should you do to increase the security of the wireless network? (Select the three best answers.)
explanation: Of the listed answers, you should make sure WPA3/AES is on if your router supports it—at least WPA2/AES if not. Then reduce the transmitting power of the AP and disable the SSID broadcast. Reducing the power prevents signal bleed to other offices; usually this can be set to “low” or something similar. Disabling the SSID or network name of the AP makes it so that a typical user cannot scan for and locate the wireless network. Other smart ideas are to put a strong password on the admin account, implement MAC filtering, and disable WPS.
whyWrong: Disabling DHCP hurts availability but does little for security.
Most SOHO routers can change channel width but cannot reduce channel availability.
QoS prioritizes traffic; it does not increase security.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 72

stem: Which of the following networking concepts describes an area that sits between the Internet and a local network, often used to host publicly accessible servers?
explanation: A screened subnet, also known as a demilitarized zone (DMZ), is an area that is not quite on the Internet and not quite part of your LAN. It’s a sort of middle ground that is for the most part protected by a firewall, but particular traffic will be let through. A screened subnet is a good place for web servers, email servers, and FTP servers because these are services required by users on the Internet.
whyWrong: NAT translates addresses as data crosses a router; it is not a network zone.
Port forwarding sends a port to an internal host; it is a mechanism, not a zone.
UPnP lets devices find each other and open ports; it is not a buffer zone.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 80

stem: You are responsible for setting up a web server and an email server on a secure part of your network, using private IP addresses. Which of the following should you implement?
explanation: Use a screened subnet (also known as a DMZ) to house the servers. This will secure them by isolating them from the LAN.
whyWrong: DHCP reservations assign fixed addresses but do not isolate servers from the LAN.
IP filtering discards certain packets but does not create a separate zone for servers.
A static WAN IP address is a public address, while these servers use private addresses.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 86

stem: While configuring a Small Office/Home Office (SOHO) device, a technician needs to ensure that the server maintains a consistent IP address at all times, following the company’s policy against static IP addresses. Which of the following options should the technician choose to achieve this requirement?
explanation: To maintain a consistent IP address for the server while adhering to the company’s policy against static IP addresses, the technician should utilize IP address reservation through DHCP. By assigning a specific IP address to the server’s MAC address within the DHCP server’s configuration, the server will always receive the same IP address when it requests an IP address lease. This approach ensures that the server is easily identifiable and accessible on the network without relying on a static IP configuration.
whyWrong: NAT translates between private and public addresses; it does not keep a server's address fixed.
DNS records map names to addresses but do not assign the address.
A VPN creates secure connections and does not assign a fixed address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 31
note: 220-1102 2.9 (IP management: DHCP reservations); DHCP reservations are not listed under 220-1202 2.10, mapped to 2.10 (router settings).

stem: A small retail store has recently set up a wireless network, but they are encountering interference from other wireless networks within proximity of the store. Which of the following actions would be MOST effective in resolving the interference with the LEAST disruption?
options: Choosing a wireless frequency that is not currently being used
Replacing the wireless equipment with Ethernet cables and switches
Regular power cycling of the equipment
explanation: The best solution for addressing interference caused by nearby SSIDs is to adjust the channel settings of your wireless network. By changing the channel, you can avoid overlapping frequencies with neighboring networks and reduce interference. This allows your wireless network to operate on a clear and less congested channel, resulting in improved performance and reduced interference issues.
whyWrong: Replacing wireless with cables disrupts the store and drops wireless devices.
Power cycling the equipment does not change the interference.
Renaming the access point does not change the frequency it uses.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 43
note: 220-1102 2.9 (wireless specific: changing channels); channel selection is not listed under 220-1202 2.10, mapped to 2.10 (wireless specific).

stem: What is the primary function of the SSID?
options: To secure communication between a web server and a browser
To secure communication between a server and a remote host
To serve as a parameter used to identify a network and configure a wireless connection
To serve as a type of password used to secure a wireless connection
explanation: A service-set identifier (SSID) is the unique name given to the wireless network. All hardware that is to participate on the network must be configured to use the same SSID. Essentially, it is the network name. When you are using Windows to connect to a wireless network, all available wireless networks will be listed by their SSID.
whyWrong: Securing traffic between a web server and a browser is the job of TLS, not of the SSID.
Securing a remote host session is done with protocols such as SSH, not with the wireless network name.
The SSID is a public network name; the security key or passphrase is what protects the connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 2
note: From a Core 1 chapter; changing the SSID is a 220-1202 2.10 topic.

stem: You have just installed a wireless router on your home network. Which of the following should you do to make it highly secure? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Change the default administrator name and password.
explanation: You should always change the default administrator name and password as well as the default SSID when installing a new wireless router. Enabling encryption is also a good idea, but WPA, WPA2, and WPA3 are better options than WEP. The channel has nothing to do with security.
whyWrong: WEP is an old, easily cracked standard; WPA2 or WPA3 should be enabled instead.
The wireless channel affects interference, not security.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 6
note: From a Core 1 chapter; SOHO router security is 220-1202 2.10.

stem: You have been asked to configure a network for a small office. The wireless router is installed, and now you need to connect the client computers. What do you enter on the client computers to connect to the router?
explanation: To join the network, client computers need to find the SSID, ensure that the security settings are correct (to match the router), and enter the security passphrase. As an administrator, you should have configured this passphrase to be different from the router's administrator password.
whyWrong: The administrator password manages the router; clients join with the wireless passphrase instead.
Clients do not type their own MAC address to join; the router reads it from the connection.
The default router password should be changed and is never what clients enter to join Wi-Fi.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 11
note: From a Core 1 chapter; wireless encryption settings are 220-1202 2.10.

stem: When enabled, which feature of a wireless router allows only specified computers to access the network?
explanation: MAC filtering is a security option that can specify that only computers with specific MAC (hardware) addresses can access the network. Port forwarding is a feature of firewalls. NAT translates private IP addresses into public ones. SSID is the wireless network name.
whyWrong: Port forwarding sends incoming traffic on a port to an inside host; it does not limit which clients join.
NAT translates private addresses to a public one; it does not choose which computers may connect.
The SSID is only the wireless network name and does not restrict access.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 16
note: From a Core 1 chapter. MAC filtering is not named in 220-1202; mapped to 2.10 router settings (filtering).

stem: What is the FIRST thing a home user should do when they purchase an IoT device such as a baby monitor?
explanation: IoT devices have default passwords that can be found on search engines. Because the device is connected to the internet, a hacker could use these publicly available passwords and gain access to your home network. Therefore, the first thing the user should do is reset the default password to something more secure.
whyWrong: Some IoT devices cannot be updated, and an update does not remove a publicly known default password.
An IoT device needs the internet to work, so disconnecting it defeats its purpose.
Reading the manual is useful, but securing the default password matters more for home security.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 14

stem: You have implemented MAC filtering on your wireless network, but some devices are still able to connect without being on the approved list. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of this issue?
options: Incorrect MAC addresses entered in the filter list
Outdated firmware on the wireless router
explanation: Incorrectly entering a MAC address in the filter list can result in devices that should be blocked being able to connect to the network. Outdated firmware on the wireless router is not related to MAC filtering. Interference from neighboring wireless networks does not affect MAC filtering.
whyWrong: Outdated firmware is a security risk, but it does not make MAC filtering let unlisted devices through.
Interference from nearby networks affects signal quality, not which devices the filter admits.
The encryption protocol is separate from MAC filtering and does not bypass the filter list.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.7 question 2
note: 220-1101 5.7 (network troubleshooting); MAC filtering is not named in 220-1202; mapped to 2.10 router settings (filtering).

stem: You have a very small network in a home-based office, and you want to limit network access to only those hosts that you physically own. What should you utilize to make this possible?
explanation: The advantage to assigning the IP addresses statically is that you can make certain which host is associated with which IP address, and then use filtering to limit network access to only those hosts. Disabling DNS will limit all hosts on a network from getting to the Internet and will not limit network access. A default subnet mask will not limit network access and will cause other problems. An empty default gateway will not limit network access.
whyWrong: Disabling DNS stops name resolution for all hosts; it does not limit which hosts can join the network.
A default subnet mask only sets the network size and does not limit access to owned hosts.
An empty default gateway only stops traffic leaving the local network; it does not limit which hosts connect.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 9

stem: Which of the following helps to secure a SOHO router? (Select the three BEST answers.)
explanation: Changing default passwords, enabling MAC filtering, and enabling the latest version of WPA can all increase the security of a SOHO router. Enabling SSID broadcast makes a router visible. Enabling WPS makes it easier to connect to the router but has security implications.
whyWrong: Enabling SSID broadcast makes the network visible; it does not add security.
WPS makes connecting easier but has known security weaknesses, so it should be disabled.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security, Cram Quiz 2 question 1

stem: You want to prevent rogue employees from connecting a laptop to the SOHO router and accessing the network. How can you accomplish this? (Select the two BEST answers.)
explanation: By enabling MAC filtering, you can create a list of MAC addresses that a SOHO router will accept. Any other computers with different MAC addresses will not be allowed access to the network. You can also disable physical ports on the router; this blocks any physical signal from being sent to those unused ports. A screened subnet (also known as a DMZ) is used to host servers and acts as a separate area between the LAN and the Internet. A complex SSID is great but won’t matter to a user connecting a laptop physically to the router because the SSID affects only wireless access.
whyWrong: A screened subnet hosts servers between the LAN and the Internet; it does not stop a laptop from connecting.
A complex SSID affects only wireless access, not a laptop plugged into the router.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security, Cram Quiz 2 question 2

stem: You want to prevent certain users from accessing particular websites. What should you configure on the SOHO router?
explanation: By enabling content filtering (and parental controls), you can select computers—by MAC address—and select what websites (domains) those computers are allowed to connect to. MAC filtering by itself simply allows or denies computers access to the router based on the MAC address of the computer. Disabling unused ports is a good idea, but it will simply stop a computer from accessing the SOHO router if it is connected on that port. Port forwarding involves configuring a router to forward Internet-based IP addresses and ports to a computer or server that is on the LAN or the screened subnet. Power levels refer to the broadcasting power of an AP’s radio.
whyWrong: MAC filtering allows or denies computers access to the router; it does not choose which websites they reach.
Disabling unused ports stops connections on those ports; it does not block particular websites.
Port forwarding sends incoming traffic to an internal computer; it does not block websites.
Power levels set how far the wireless signal reaches; they do not control which websites users visit.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security, Cram Quiz 2 question 3

stem: A network technician is following a checklist that involves updating firmware on all company SOHO routers. What is the purpose of firmware updates on a SOHO router?
options: To improve router performance and stability
To add new features and functionalities
To fix security vulnerabilities and bugs
explanation: Firmware updates on a small office/home office (SOHO) router serve multiple purposes. Firstly, they aim to improve the overall performance and stability of the router, ensuring it runs smoothly and efficiently. Secondly, firmware updates can introduce new features and functionalities, enhancing the router’s capabilities. Lastly, and most importantly, firmware updates often address security vulnerabilities and bugs, providing necessary patches to safeguard against potential attacks or unauthorized access.
whyWrong: Performance and stability are only one purpose, so this choice alone does not answer fully.
New features are only one purpose, so this choice alone does not answer fully.
Security fixes are the most important purpose but not the only one, so this choice is incomplete.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.9 question 1

stem: A technician is helping a user to configure their home router. The wireless router is new and has not been configured. In the first instance, the technician wants to configure the network interface with the correct IP address supplied by the internet service provider (ISP). What configuration option should they choose?
options: Create Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) reservations
Configure the static wide-area network (WAN) IP
explanation: A static wide-area network (WAN) IP, also known as a static public IP, is a fixed internet protocol (IP) address assigned to a device or network that is connected to the internet via a wide-area network. The ISP supplies this address, and it is set on the router’s WAN interface.
whyWrong: DHCP reservations give internal devices such as printers a fixed address; they do not set the WAN address.
UPnP lets internal devices such as game consoles open firewall ports, not set the ISP address.
A screened subnet is only needed for an internet-facing service such as an FTP server.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.9 question 2
note: 220-1102 2.9 (static WAN IP); mapped to 220-1202 2.10 (router settings). Static WAN IP is no longer listed in 220-1202.

stem: A home user is having difficulty connecting their PlayStation gaming system to the internet gaming service. The user thinks that the router may be blocking the gaming system from accessing the internet service. What feature would allow the user to access the internet gaming service?
options: Disable content filtering on the router
Disable Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) on the router
Enable Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) on the router
explanation: UPnP is a protocol that allows devices on a network to discover and communicate with each other without requiring a user to perform manual configuration. This simplifies tasks such as port opening for online gaming and accessing printers, media servers, and smart TVs.
