whyWrong: Content filtering blocks inappropriate web pages and email; it is not what blocks the game service.
Disabling DHCP does not change the firewall rules that block the gaming service.
A screened subnet is for hosting public servers and is not needed for a game console.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.9 question 3

stem: A small print shop wants to host an FTP server to allow customers to upload documents that can then be printed as part of the service. The intention is to use a computer that has access to the internet. The print shop has a SOHO wireless router only. What feature will allow this service to be securely hosted? (Choose two.)
options: Configure IP filtering to protect the customer-facing FTP server
Configure a screened subnet to place the customer-facing computer
Configure firmware updates on the router
Configure port forwarding to route traffic from the internet to the FTP server
explanation: A screened subnet allows a semi-secure zone where a hardened host server can be placed. The server will be accessed from the internet through the firewall and will also be accessible from the internal network. Port forwarding will ensure the requests sent by external customers to the WAN IP address are routed correctly to the FTP server on the screened subnet.
whyWrong: IP filtering is of little use here, as there would be only one IP address in the screened subnet.
Firmware updates keep the router current but do not let customers reach the FTP server.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.9 question 4
note: 220-1102 2.9; mapped to 220-1202 2.10 (SOHO network security). The book key gives only B, but the question says Choose two and its explanation also gives port forwarding (D), so the answer is B and D.

stem: A technician is helping a user to configure their Wi-Fi home router. The wireless router is new and has not been configured. The technician wants to secure the device against the threat of unauthorized connections. What two settings would be most effective? (Choose two.)
explanation: Without broadcasting the assigned wireless network identifier, an attacker will have to use specialist equipment to detect the presence of the network. Manufacturers of network equipment use standard default administrator account names and passwords on products. These should always be changed.
whyWrong: A screened subnet is for internet-facing servers such as FTP or web, which are not needed here.
Guest access is not needed here and would reduce the security of the router.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.9 question 5

stem: A sales outlet in a shopping mall is experiencing latency on the wireless network. Staff are complaining that when they are demonstrating features on phones and tablets, the devices appear very slow to display pages. A technician notices that there are many other wireless networks in close proximity. What may offer a solution for a better-quality wireless signal?
explanation: In an area where there may be multiple wireless access points deployed, it is worthwhile investigating whether there are channels that are unused or have less congestion. Wireless controllers using the 2.4 GHz range only have the option for three non-overlapping channels.
whyWrong: Disabling SSID broadcast is a security setting and does not reduce interference from nearby networks.
Encryption settings affect security, not the congestion caused by nearby networks.
Disabling guest access is a security setting and does not improve signal quality.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.9 question 6
note: 220-1102 2.9; mapped to 220-1202 2.10 (wireless settings). Changing channels is not listed in 220-1202 2.10.

stem: A network technician is assisting a coffee shop with establishing a wireless network for customers to use. The shop intends to print a passkey onto sales receipts so that customers can access free Wi-Fi. The technician is asked to secure the network so that only legitimate customers can securely use the network. What security setting would be BEST for these requirements?
explanation: In a small business, such as a coffee shop, it is common to share the passkey with customers to provide access to free Wi-Fi. The most secure way to do this is to use simultaneous authentication of equals (SAE). This uses AES encryption and prevents brute-force attacks against the key.
whyWrong: WEP has been discontinued and is not secure.
WPA2 does not support SAE, and TKIP is an old, weak encryption method.
WPA2-AES uses a preshared key without SAE, so it is weaker than WPA3-SAE.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.9 question 7
note: 220-1102 2.9; mapped to 220-1202 2.10 (wireless encryption settings). The book says SAE uses AES 256-bit; WPA3-Personal uses 128-bit AES, so the bit length is removed from the explanation.

stem: A dentist's office runs a public appointment web server and a file server with patient records behind one SOHO router. The owner wants patients to reach the web server from the Internet without any route to the file server. Which configuration is the BEST choice?
options: Place the web server in a screened subnet
Turn on the router's content filter
explanation: A screened subnet, or DMZ, holds public-facing servers in a zone that Internet users can reach while firewall rules keep them out of the LAN. The file server stays on the internal network with no inbound path.
whyWrong: UPnP lets devices open ports on their own, which adds risk and does not separate the servers.
Hiding the network name affects wireless discovery, not Internet access to a server.
A content filter limits which sites internal users visit; it does not control inbound access to servers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

stem: A technician unpacks a new wireless router for a home office and logs in to its web page at 192.168.0.1 with the login printed in the manual. Which change should the technician make FIRST?
explanation: Default logins for router models are published online, so anyone on the network could take control of the device. Changing the admin password comes before any other setting.
whyWrong: Changing the channel can reduce interference, but it does nothing to stop someone from logging in with the default credentials.
Port forwarding opens inbound access and is only set up when a service needs it, never before the device is secured.
A guest network is useful for visitors, but the admin login must be secured before other features are added.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

stem: A small shop owner wants to harden the store's SOHO router after a security review. The review notes that WPS is on, the network uses WPA2 with TKIP, and four LAN ports are unused. Which TWO changes will improve security? (Choose two.)
options: Switch the wireless security to WPA3
Raise the radio power level to high
explanation: Disabled ports stop a rogue device from getting access when it is plugged into a spare jack. WPA3 replaces deprecated TKIP with the current Wi-Fi security standard. Both reduce the ways an attacker can join the network.
whyWrong: UPnP lets devices open ports automatically, so turning it on weakens the firewall.
Broadcasting the network name makes the network easier to find, which does not add protection.
Higher power spreads the signal farther outside the building, which helps outsiders reach the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

stem: Which of the following are recommended general browser security procedures for an organization to implement? (Select three answers.)
options: Mandate the use of specific web browsers across all departments.
Implement policies to manage add-ons and restrict access to malicious websites.
Train users on safe browsing habits and how to handle pop-ups.
Rely solely on built-in browser security features without additional configurations.
Use a proxy and content filter to cache websites and block potentially harmful sites.
Disable all JavaScript to prevent malicious code execution.
explanation: Policies can be configured to manage add-ons and disallow access to websites that are known to be malicious. User training is also important when it comes to helping users know which websites to access, how to use search engines, and what to do if pop-ups appear onscreen. In addition, use a proxy and content filter to cache websites and block potentially harmful sites.
whyWrong: Mandating one browser may be part of a strategy, but it is not a general browser security procedure.
Relying only on built-in features without configuration is not enough.
Disabling all JavaScript would break many legitimate websites.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 91

stem:
An open source software build is downloaded from the GitHub repository. Prior to installing the software image, a technician encounters the following string:

7d3bb8e188cd9154e99b7ea8db38a24181efb2d1

Which option MOST accurately describes the intended use of this string?
options: Checksum for verification of download integrity
explanation: This string is most likely a checksum or hash value. It is used to verify the integrity of the downloaded software image. By comparing the calculated checksum of the downloaded file to this value, the technician can ensure that the file has not been tampered with during the download process.
whyWrong: An encryption key encrypts and decrypts data; it is not used to check a download.
A product license key activates software and does not look like a hash.
A network port number is a small number, not a long hexadecimal string.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 23
note: 220-1102 2.10; mapped to 220-1202 2.11 (browser download/installation: trusted sources, hashing). The staging options were broken (the hash and the stem's last line were parsed as options A and B); the stem and the four real options were rebuilt.

stem: A sales manager has been unable to access a website and has submitted a help desk ticket. The website that is causing the problem for the manager has been verified to be online. Which of the following troubleshooting steps will MOST LIKELY resolve the issue?
explanation: If the website has been verified to be online, the most likely cause of the issue lies with the user’s browser. By deleting the browser history, any cached data or cookies that might be causing conflicts or preventing access to the website can be cleared, potentially resolving the issue.
whyWrong: Clearing the DNS cache helps with name resolution problems, while the site itself is reachable.
Flushing the ARP cache addresses local network problems, not a browser problem.
JavaScript is not related to whether the browser can reach one website.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 52
note: 220-1102 2.10 (clearing browsing data, clearing cache); mapped to 220-1202 2.11 (settings).

stem: Safari, Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome, and Microsoft Edge are all examples of what?
explanation: All these programs are Web browsers. A web browser is the client program that requests and displays web pages from web servers.
whyWrong: A web server hosts websites; these programs are clients that display them.
A print server manages print jobs for shared printers.
A proxy server forwards requests for clients; these programs are the clients themselves.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 18: Essentials of Networking, Chapter Review question 7

stem: Which of these is a password manager?
explanation: The Windows Credential Manager is a password manager that is built into the operating system of Windows. Edge and Internet Explorer 11 work in conjunction with the Credential Manager, but they are not password managers. Active Directory is used to authenticate domain users, but it does not manage passwords for end users.
whyWrong: Edge is a web browser that works with Credential Manager; it is not a password manager itself.
Internet Explorer 11 is an old web browser, not a password manager.
Active Directory authenticates domain users; it does not store passwords for end users.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 8

stem: Which type of add-on will extend the functionality of the web browser in a way it wasn’t originally designed?
explanation: An extension is a type of add-on that will extend the functionality of the web browser in a way it was never originally designed. A pop-up blocker changed the way a web page is rendered. A plug-in changes the way a web page is rendered. An ad blocker also changes the way a web page is rendered.
whyWrong: A pop-up blocker only stops pop-up windows; it does not add new functions to the browser.
A plug-in changes how a page's content is rendered rather than adding new browser functions.
An ad blocker changes how a page is rendered by hiding ads; it does not add new functions.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems, Review Questions question 11

stem: Which of the following are used to prevent pop-unders from appearing?
explanation: Pop-up blockers are used to prevent pop-ups and pop-unders from appearing. Antimalware utilities will remove and prevent malware. Phishing sites are used to collect users credentials' by tricking users. Antivirus software is used to protect the operating system from viruses.
whyWrong: Antimalware utilities remove and prevent malware; they do not block pop-under windows.
Phishing sites trick users into giving credentials; they cause problems rather than prevent them.
Antivirus software protects the operating system from viruses; it does not block pop-under windows.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 9

stem: You have been tasked with implementing ad-blocking functionality within a web browser. Which of the following should you add to make ad blocking a reality?
explanation: Add an extension for the ad blocker of your choice. (Make sure it’s relatively secure!) A valid certificate is required before a web browser establishes a session with a web server. Pop-up blockers are different from ad blockers in that they block pop-up windows in general; an ad blocker might happen to block some pop-up windows but only because they are ad based. A password manager stores passwords in an encrypted fashion within a vault on the local computer.
whyWrong: A valid certificate is needed to set up a secure session with a web server; it does not block ads.
A pop-up blocker blocks pop-up windows in general, not ads inside web pages.
A password manager stores passwords in an encrypted vault; it does not block ads.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: A user’s computer is running very slow. You investigate and find out that there are many, many temporary files, caused by excessive browsing. Where would you go in Microsoft Edge to fix the problem?
explanation: In the address bar, go to edge://settings/privacy and then click Clear browsing data. This will remove all of the temporary files that are potentially slowing down the system. edge://settings/profiles/sync is used for sign-in and data synchronization. chrome://extensions is where you would go to enable or disable extensions in Chrome, not Microsoft Edge. edge://settings/content is for blocking pop-ups.
whyWrong: edge://settings/profiles/sync is for sign-in and data synchronization, not for clearing browsing data.
chrome://extensions manages extensions in Chrome, not in Microsoft Edge.
edge://settings/content is for site permissions such as pop-up blocking, not for clearing browsing data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You want to verify that Google Chrome will connect to websites in a secure manner. Where should you go to confirm this? (Select the two BEST answers.)
options: Installation file signature from a trusted source
Trusted zones in Internet Properties > Security
explanation: Check the TLS setting in Internet Properties > Advanced. In most cases, you want to make sure that it is TLS 1.2 or higher. Also, check out the trusted zones section of Internet Properties > Security. This is where you can select the level of security and specify custom levels, if necessary. Both of these will work for Edge and for Chrome.
whyWrong: A PGP key verifies that an installation file was not tampered with; it does not affect secure connections.
An installation file signature checks the browser download, not how the browser connects to websites.
Incognito mode keeps session data from being stored locally; it does not make connections more secure.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: You are working for Geeks of the Future, a company that solves home user technology issues. One customer’s computer is suffering from slow performance as well as browser crashes. These issues began after the customer clicked a “repair” pop-up while browsing the Web. Which of the following should you perform FIRST to resolve the issue? (Select the two best answers.)
options: Enable the web browser’s pop-up blocker.
Scan the storage drive’s boot sector and RAM with an antivirus program.
Initiate a cold shutdown and then turn on the computer.
Uninstall any recently installed suspicious programs and browser extensions.
Run SFC and replace changed files with the original system files.
explanation: The first things you should do are to enable the web browser’s pop-up blocker and uninstall any recently installed suspicious programs and browser extensions. The problem occurred when the customer clicked on a fake repair pop-up while browsing the Internet. The act of clicking the pop-up probably initiated more problems—for example, the installation of unwanted browser extensions (which is common) or perhaps even undesirable programs. These extensions and/or programs are most likely causing the system to behave slowly because they are reaching out to the Internet to do malicious things. And the very first thing you should do if malware is even a remote consideration is to quarantine or isolate the system.
whyWrong: Scanning only the boot sector and RAM with antivirus software is not enough; the whole system needs an antimalware scan.
A cold shutdown and restart helps with some issues but does not remove unwanted extensions or programs.
SFC repairs operating system files, which might be needed later, but it is not the first step here.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security, Cram Quiz question 4
note: The book's explanation adds that quarantining the system is the very first step when malware is suspected; that option is not offered.

stem: How are updates for the Safari web browser typically managed?
options: Through the browser's built-in settings menu, similar to Chrome and Firefox
Independently by downloading patch files directly from Apple's website
As part of the macOS system update process
By manually installing updates prompted by the browser itself
explanation: Safari updates are managed through the macOS system update mechanism, ensuring the browser is patched along with the operating system. However, Chrome and Firefox update automatically or via their settings menus. Apple does macOS systems updates and usually does not offer patch file updates.
whyWrong: Chrome and Firefox update through their own settings, but Safari is updated with macOS.
Apple does not usually offer separate patch files for Safari on its website.
Safari does not install its own prompted updates; its updates come through macOS system updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: What is the primary security benefit of using Secure DNS?
options: It speeds up website loading times by caching DNS requests.
It prevents third parties from intercepting and manipulating DNS requests.
It blocks advertisements and prevents tracking of browsing habits.
It automatically updates web browsers to the latest secure versions.
explanation: Secure DNS encrypts your DNS requests to prevent eavesdropping and manipulation by third parties to enhance privacy and security. Yes, caching DNS requests can speed up website load times, but note that is not the security benefit. Many third-party DNS services do block advertisements and prevent tracking, which is great but again not necessarily a security benefit. DNS is just to look up domain names to IP addresses; it doesn't update your browser.
whyWrong: Caching DNS requests can speed up page loads, but that is not a security benefit of Secure DNS.
Some DNS services block ads and tracking, but that is not the security benefit of Secure DNS.
DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses; it does not update web browsers.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: A user's Chrome menu icon has changed to show that an update has downloaded. The user keeps working and ignores it. What must happen for the update to be applied?
options: The user must relaunch the browser
The user must reinstall Chrome from its website
The user must clear the browser cache
The user must sign in to browser sync
explanation: Chrome downloads updates silently in the background and then shows a change on its menu icon. The update is applied when the browser closes and reopens. An administrator can also set a policy that forces users to relaunch within a set time.
whyWrong: Reinstalling is not needed, because the update has already downloaded and only needs a relaunch.
Clearing the cache removes stored web files and does not install a browser update.
Sign-in and sync share bookmarks and passwords between devices; they do not apply updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

stem: A company bans saving website passwords in Google Chrome. A technician must turn off both the offer to save passwords and password autofill. Which address opens the correct settings page?
explanation: Chrome's built-in password manager is set up under Settings, Autofill, Passwords, which also opens at chrome://settings/passwords. There the technician turns off the offer to save passwords and the automatic sign-in that fills them in. In Edge, the matching page is edge://settings/passwords.
whyWrong: chrome://extensions manages installed extensions, not the browser's own password manager settings.
chrome://flags holds experimental features and is not where saved passwords are controlled.
That page deletes browsing data but does not stop Chrome from offering to save passwords later.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security

stem: A company web app shows broken pages in Microsoft Edge on one user's PC but works on other PCs. The user has many extensions installed. Which action BEST tests whether an extension causes the problem?
options: Turn off all extensions in edge://extensions and reload the page
Turn on experimental features in edge://flags
Turn off the pop-up blocker for all sites
Change the proxy server in the network settings
explanation: Extensions interact with the pages that the browser renders, so one of them can break a site. Turning all extensions off with their toggles on the extensions page and reloading shows whether an extension is the cause. If the page then works, the technician turns the extensions back on one at a time to find the bad one.
whyWrong: The flags page holds experimental features that can cause new problems; it does not isolate extensions.
Turning off the pop-up blocker lowers security and does not test whether an extension breaks pages.
The app works on other PCs, so a proxy change does not test the user's installed extensions.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

stem: A technician is advising a customer who requires assistance with the installation of a web browser. For ease of use, the user would prefer to download and install a browser that did not come installed with the default OS. What two pieces of advice can the technician offer the user to ensure a safe installation?
options: Make sure to download the browser from trusted sources
After download, check that the file size is identical to the file size on the vendor site
Make sure to download a browser with a password manager
After download, check that the hash value is identical to the value published on the vendor site
explanation: When installing new software, it is recommended to always use a trusted site. If a user wants to download Google Chrome, for example, then it is best to visit the vendor site, not a third-party unknown site. Many software vendors publish the hash, or checksum, for the download file. This can be verified using a hashing utility on the user’s workstation.
whyWrong: A malicious download file could be the same size as the genuine one, so size proves little.
A password manager is a useful feature but does not make the download or installation safe.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.10 question 1

stem: A company would like to allow users to view websites that are not automatically translated into the user’s native language. Presently, users are complaining that they need to copy and paste the content into the word processing application to perform translation. What can the company do to BEST help the users?
options: Add a language translator as a browser extension
Install a new browser that supports language translation
Add support for additional languages to the Windows settings menu
explanation: Adding a language translator as a browser extension is the most convenient and user-friendly solution for the company to help users translate websites into their native language. Browser extensions, such as Google Translate, allow users to translate web content directly within the browser without the need to copy and paste the content into a separate application.
whyWrong: An extension gives the same function without making users switch to a new browser.
HTML5 support is important for modern sites but does not translate any web pages.
Adding Windows display languages does not translate the content of websites.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.10 question 2

stem: A support desk operator has been assigned a support ticket raised by a user who complains that web pages take too long to load and seem to display a lot of advertising content within the pages. What will be the BEST solution to speed up the user’s browser when displaying web pages?
explanation: By enabling an ad blocker, the browser will be able to render and display web pages much quicker. The advertising content embedded in the pages is not downloaded or displayed.
whyWrong: Pop-up blockers stop separate windows, but most advertising is now embedded within the pages.
Clearing the browsing cache does not block advertising content on web pages.
Private-browsing mode only stops history being kept and does not block ads.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.10 question 3

stem: A customer asks a support technician how can they be sure that the banking website can be trusted. They have been told that fake sites can be made to resemble genuine sites. What ensures that a website can be trusted?
options: The site will display a padlock when connecting using HTTPS
Ensure there is a trusted certificate when connecting using HTTP
The site will display a security rating when connecting using HTTPS
Ensure to always connect using private-browsing mode
explanation: When browsing websites that are secure, the client browser will display a padlock symbol to show the user that the site has a valid certificate. The certificate shows that the connection is encrypted and that the site name matches the certificate.
whyWrong: Plain HTTP does not use certificates, so there is no certificate to check.
Browsers do not display a security rating for HTTPS sites.
Private-browsing mode only stops history being kept and says nothing about the site’s identity.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 8: Security, Objective 2.10 question 4
note: 220-1102 2.10; mapped to 220-1202 2.11 (secure connections and valid certificates). A padlock shows a valid certificate and an encrypted connection, but fake sites can also get certificates, so it does not prove a site can be trusted.

stem: After installing a free PDF converter, a user finds that the browser's home page and search engine have changed and a new toolbar has appeared. Which of the following is the MOST LIKELY cause?
options: An extension from an untrusted source
explanation: Free software from untrusted sources often installs browser extensions that change the home page and search settings. Such extensions can also collect data and slow the system. Removing the extension and resetting the browser fixes the changes.
whyWrong: An expired certificate causes a warning on one site; it does not change the home page or add a toolbar.
A full cache can slow page loading, but it does not change browser settings or add toolbars.
Without a pop-up blocker, extra windows appear, but the home page and search engine would not change.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security

stem: A technician stores an offline browser installer on a network share for future installs. Months later, the technician wants to confirm that nobody altered the file before using it. Which action is the BEST choice?
options: Compare its SHA256 hash with the value recorded when it was downloaded
Check the file's modified date in File Explorer
Scan the file share with Disk Cleanup
Open the installer in private-browsing mode
explanation: Any change to a file changes its hash, so a hash that matches the stored value shows the file is unchanged. In Windows, the PowerShell Get-FileHash cmdlet computes the value.
whyWrong: A modified date can be changed or kept the same, so it does not prove the file was not tampered with.
Disk Cleanup removes temporary files and does not verify that a file is intact.
Private-browsing mode controls stored browsing data and cannot check an installer file.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

stem: A sales rep often works from airport and hotel Wi-Fi and is worried that others on those networks can see which websites the browser looks up. Which browser setting will BEST address this concern?
explanation: Normal DNS queries travel in plain text, so others on the network can read or alter them. Secure DNS, also called DNS over HTTPS, encrypts the lookups. It is set in the browser's privacy and security settings.
whyWrong: A pop-up blocker stops extra windows; it does not protect the browser's name lookups.
Synchronization copies browser data between devices and does not encrypt lookups on the network.
Clearing the cache removes stored page files on the computer but leaves network lookups unprotected.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems
